title.zh: 卷232 列傳十九 希福 范文程 甯完我 鲍承先
title.en: Volume 232 Biographies 19: Xi Fu, Fan Wencheng, Ning Wan Wo, Bao Chengxian
title.raw: 卷232 列傳十九 希福 范文程 甯完我 鲍承先

sentences.zh: 希福，赫舍里氏。

translations.literal: Xi Fu, of the Hesheri clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fu was of the Hesheri clan.

sentences.zh: 世居都英額，再遷哈達。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt at Duying'e, and moved again to Hada.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long lived at Duying'e before moving once more to Hada.

sentences.zh: 太祖既滅哈達，希福從其兄碩色率所部來歸。

translations.literal: After the Grand Ancestor had destroyed Hada, Xi Fu followed his elder brother Shuo Se and led their following to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu Emperor had conquered Hada, Xi Fu came over with his elder brother Shuo Se at the head of their followers.

sentences.zh: 居有頃，以希福兼通滿、漢、蒙古文字，召直文館。

translations.literal: After a short time, because Xi Fu was versed in Manchu, Chinese, and Mongol scripts, he was summoned to serve in the Literary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xi Fu's command of Manchu, Chinese, and Mongol writing earned him a post on the staff of the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 屢奉使蒙古諸部，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly sent as envoy to the Mongol tribes and was granted the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched repeatedly to the Mongol tribes and honored with the title "Bakshi."

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正黃旗。

translations.literal: When the banner system was fixed, he was registered under the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were formally organized, he was assigned to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰二年，太宗伐察哈爾，以希福使科爾沁徵兵，土謝圖額駙奧巴止之曰：「寇騎塞路，行將安之？

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancong, the Taizong Emperor campaigned against the Chahar; Xi Fu was sent to the Khorchin to levy troops. Tushetu Efu Oba tried to stop him, saying: "Enemy horsemen block the road—where can you go?
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancong, Hong Taiji marched against the Chahar and dispatched Xi Fu to the Khorchin to muster troops. Tushetu Efu Oba urged him to turn back: "Enemy cavalry have sealed the roads—where do you mean to go?

sentences.zh: 即有失，誰執其咎？」

translations.literal: If there should be any mishap, who will bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: If something goes wrong, who will answer for it?"

sentences.zh: 希福曰：「君命安得辭？

translations.literal: Xi Fu said: "How can one decline a sovereign's command?
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fu replied: "How can one refuse an imperial order?

sentences.zh: 死則死耳，事不可誤也。」

translations.literal: If I must die, then die I shall; the mission must not be failed."
translations.idiomatic: Death is death—but the task must not fail."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: With that, he set out.
translations.idiomatic: And he went.

sentences.zh: 再宿，達上所，復命曰：「科爾沁兵不赴徵，土謝圖額駙奧巴方率所部行掠，掠竟乃來耳。」

translations.literal: After two nights' travel he reached the sovereign and reported: "The Khorchin have not answered the levy; Tushetu Efu Oba is even now leading his men on a raid and will come only when the raid is finished."
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he reached the court and reported: "The Khorchin would not muster, and Tushetu Efu Oba was off raiding with his forces and would join only when the raiding was done."

sentences.zh: 上怒，使希福再往，以壯士八人從。

translations.literal: The sovereign was enraged and sent Xi Fu again, with eight stalwart men as escort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sent Xi Fu back, attended by eight brave men.

sentences.zh: 行四晝夜，道遇敵，擊殺三十餘人，卒至科爾沁，以其兵來會。

translations.literal: After four days and nights on the road they met the enemy, killed more than thirty, and at last reached the Khorchin and brought their troops to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: Four days and nights later they met enemy forces on the road, killed more than thirty, and finally reached the Khorchin and brought their troops into the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 明年，奧巴來朝，上命希福與館臣庫爾纏輩責讓之，奧巴服罪，上駝馬以謝。

translations.literal: The next year Oba came to court; the sovereign ordered Xi Fu and the secretariat officials such as Kuruchan to rebuke him. Oba pleaded guilty and presented camels and horses in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Oba came to pay tribute. The emperor had Xi Fu and secretariat officials including Kuruchan rebuke him. Oba acknowledged his fault and sent camels and horses in apology.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授備禦。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was appointed Beyu.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Beyu.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，薄明都，敗明兵於城下。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Ming, pressed close to the Ming capital, and defeated Ming troops below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Ming, drew near the Ming capital, and routed Ming forces beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 攻大凌河，援兵自錦州至，與譚泰爭先奮擊，破之。

translations.literal: At the assault on Dalinghe, relief troops came from Jinzhou; he strove with Tan Tai to strike first and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dalinghe was besieged and relief came from Jinzhou, he vied with Tan Tai to lead the charge and crushed the relief force.

sentences.zh: 師還，又力戰敗追兵，進游擊。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again fought hard and defeated pursuing troops, and was advanced to Guerrilla Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he again fought fiercely and beat off pursuers, and was promoted to guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，改文館為內三院，希福為內國史院承政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde the Literary Bureau was renamed the Three Inner Courts; Xi Fu became Chancellor of the Inner History Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde the Literary Bureau became the Three Inner Courts, and Xi Fu was made chancellor of the Inner History Court.

sentences.zh: 尋授內弘文院大學士，進二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Inner Council of Culture and advanced to second-rank jalan gūsa-i janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand secretary of the Inner Council of Culture and promoted to second-rank jalan gūsa-i janggin.

sentences.zh: 二年，請禁造言惑眾，違者罪之，著為令。

translations.literal: In the second year he petitioned to forbid rumor-mongering that misled the people; violators were to be punished, and this was enacted as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he urged a ban on seditious rumor, with penalties for violators, and the measure was promulgated as law.

sentences.zh: 三年，偕大學士范文程建言定部院官制。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng, he proposed fixing the official system of the ministries and courts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng in recommending a formal organization for the ministries and courts.

sentences.zh: 希福雖以文學事上，官內院，筦機務，然常出使察哈爾、喀爾喀、科爾沁諸部，編戶口，置牛錄，頒法律，亭平獄訟；

translations.literal: Although Xi Fu served the sovereign through letters and held office in the inner courts managing state affairs, he was often sent as envoy to the Chahar, Khalkha, Khorchin, and other tribes to register households, establish niru, promulgate laws, and settle lawsuits impartially;
translations.idiomatic: Though Xi Fu served the throne as a scholar-official in the inner courts and handled weighty affairs of state, he was often dispatched to the Chahar, Khalkha, Khorchin, and other tribes to register households, establish niru, promulgate laws, and adjudicate disputes fairly;

sentences.zh: 時或詣軍前宣示機宜，相度形勢，覈諸將戰閥，行賞，諭上德意於諸降人。

translations.literal: at times he would go to the front to explain strategy, survey the terrain, verify the generals' battle records, distribute rewards, and convey the sovereign's gracious intent to those who had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: at times he went to the front to explain strategy, survey the terrain, verify commanders' battle records, distribute rewards, and convey the emperor's benevolent intent to those who had submitted.

sentences.zh: 每還奏，未嘗不稱旨也。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned and reported, his words never failed to please the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Every report he brought back won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，譯遼、金、元三史成，奏進，世祖恩賚有加。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the translation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Yuan was completed; he presented it to the throne and the Shizu Emperor bestowed extra favors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi the translation of the Liao, Jin, and Yuan histories was finished; he presented it to the throne and the Shunzhi Emperor rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 希福故與譚泰有隙，屢誚其衰慵。

translations.literal: Xi Fu had long been at odds with Tan Tai and repeatedly mocked him as senile and indolent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fu had long been at odds with Tan Tai and often ridiculed him as feeble and slack.

sentences.zh: 譚泰暱附攝政睿親王多爾袞，因與其弟譚布構希福妄傳王語，謂堂餐過侈，詆謾諸大臣，構釁亂政，罪當死；

translations.literal: Tan Tai was close to the Prince Regent, Prince Rui Dorgon; he and his younger brother Tan Bu therefore framed Xi Fu for falsely spreading the prince's words, claiming that court meals were too lavish, slandering the ministers, and stirring strife to disrupt government—an offense deserving death;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai was close to the Prince Regent Dorgon; he and his younger brother Tan Bu then framed Xi Fu for falsely attributing words to the prince, alleging extravagant court banquets, slandering senior ministers, and fomenting disorder in government—an offense punishable by death;

sentences.zh: 王命罷官削世職，並籍其家。

translations.literal: the prince ordered him dismissed from office, stripped of his hereditary rank, and his household confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: the prince ordered him dismissed, stripped of his hereditary rank, and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，世祖親政，雪其枉，仍授內弘文院大學士，复世職。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year the Shizu Emperor took personal rule, cleared his wrongful conviction, and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Inner Council of Culture and restored his hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year the Shunzhi Emperor assumed personal rule, cleared his wrongful conviction, restored him as grand secretary of the Inner Council of Culture, and reinstated his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 九年，世祖以希福事太祖、太宗，銜命馳驅，殫心力。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Shizu Emperor noted that Xi Fu had served the Taizu and Taizong emperors, racing on imperial orders and exhausting his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor noted that Xi Fu had served the Taizu and Taizong emperors at a gallop on every commission, giving his utmost.

sentences.zh: 曩定鼎燕京，希福方削籍，功未賞，乃一歲三進為三等精奇尼哈番，世襲。

translations.literal: When the capital had been fixed at Yanjing, Xi Fu had been struck from the rolls and his merits went unrewarded; now within one year he was thrice advanced to third-rank jingqini hafan, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital had been fixed at Beijing his merits had gone unrewarded because he had been disgraced; now within a single year he was promoted three times to third-rank jingqini hafan, hereditary.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，卒，贈太保，諡文簡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he died; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of that year and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 長子奇塔特，襲職。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qitata inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qitata inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封三等子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign his enfeoffment was fixed as third-rank zi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign the family rank was fixed as third-rank zi.

sentences.zh: 帥顏保，希福次子。

translations.literal: Shuaibao, Xi Fu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Shuaibao was Xi Fu's second son.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，聖祖念希福事先朝久，躬預佐命，用大學士范文程、額色黑例，超授內國史院學士。

translations.literal: Early in the Kangxi reign the Sage Ancestor, recalling that Xi Fu had long served the previous dynasty and personally aided in establishing the mandate, followed the precedent of Grand Secretaries Fan Wencheng and Esheihei and exceptionally appointed him Bachelor of the Inner History Court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign the emperor, remembering Xi Fu's long service to the founding court, followed the precedent set for Fan Wencheng and Esheihei and exceptionally appointed Shuaibao bachelor of the Inner History Court.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year he was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 七月，授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 九月，疏言：「淮安水陸孔道，乃十五里中為關者三，板閘有鈔關，淮安有倉稅，隸戶部；

translations.literal: In the ninth month he memorialized: "The land and water thoroughfare at Huai'an has three passes within fifteen li; at Banzha there is a transit duty office, and at Huai'an there is a granary tax, both under the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he memorialized: "The land and water route at Huai'an has three customs posts within fifteen li; Banzha has a transit duty office and Huai'an a granary tax, both under the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 清江有稅廠，隸工部。

translations.literal: at Qingjiang there is a tax station under the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Qingjiang has a tax station under the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 胥役繁冗，商民耗資失時，請減三為一，合併稅額，省胥役，便商民。」

translations.literal: Clerks and runners are numerous, merchants lose money and time—I beg to reduce the three to one, merge the tax quotas, cut clerks, and ease matters for merchants."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and runners are too numerous, and merchants lose money and time. I ask that the three be reduced to one, the tax quotas merged, clerks cut, and commerce eased."

sentences.zh: 下部議，戶部言倉稅並鈔關便；

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for deliberation; the Ministry of Revenue said merging the granary tax with the transit office would be convenient;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred for deliberation; the Ministry of Revenue favored merging the granary tax with the transit office;

sentences.zh: 工部言稅廠徵船料諸稅，葺治漕船，並鈔關不便。

translations.literal: the Ministry of Works said the tax station levies ship-material and other duties to repair grain-transport vessels, and merging with the transit office would be inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: the Ministry of Works objected that the tax station levies ship-material and other duties to repair grain-transport vessels, and that merging it with the transit office would be impractical.

sentences.zh: 上心韙帥顏保言，下九卿科道再議，卒如所請。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved Shuaibao's proposal in his heart and ordered the Nine Ministers and the censorate to deliberate again; in the end it was done as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Shuaibao's proposal and ordered the Nine Ministers and the censorate to reconsider; in the end his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，疏言：「淮、揚被水，高郵、宿遷、桃源、鹽城、贛榆災尤重。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he memorialized: "Huai and Yang have suffered flooding; Gaoyou, Suqian, Taoyuan, Yancheng, and Ganyu have been hit especially hard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he memorialized: "Huai and Yang have been flooded; Gaoyou, Suqian, Taoyuan, Yancheng, and Ganyu have suffered especially severe damage.

sentences.zh: 舊逋漕米，例當補徵，民力不能勝。」

translations.literal: Arrears in tribute grain are by rule to be levied in full, but the people's strength cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Arrears in tribute grain must by rule be collected in full, but the people cannot bear the burden."

sentences.zh: 下部議，請改折，仍補徵。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down; the ministries proposed commutation to silver but still collection of arrears.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred for deliberation; the ministries proposed commutation to silver but still insisted on collecting the arrears.

sentences.zh: 上以諸縣頻歲被災，民重困，下部再議，免舊逋漕米三萬一千石有奇。

translations.literal: The sovereign, noting that these counties had suffered disaster year after year and the people were sorely afflicted, sent the matter down again; more than thirty-one thousand shi of old tribute-grain arrears were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting that these counties had suffered repeated disasters and the people were in dire straits, ordered further deliberation; more than thirty-one thousand shi of old tribute-grain arrears were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，偕河道總督王光裕疏請漕運畢事，當復舊例，舉劾所屬文武官吏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, together with Director-General of Rivers Wang Guangyu, he memorialized that when grain transport was finished the old practice of commending and impeaching subordinate civil and military officials should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he joined River Director-General Wang Guangyu in asking that, once the grain transport season was complete, the old practice of commending and impeaching subordinate civil and military officials be restored.

sentences.zh: 既得請，疏薦山東糧道遲日巽、河南糧道範週、無錫知縣吳興祚等，劾溧陽知縣王錫範等。

translations.literal: After his request was granted, he memorialized to recommend Shandong Grain Intendant Chi Rixun, Henan Grain Intendant Fan Zhou, Wuxi Magistrate Wu Xingzuo, and others, and to impeach Liyang Magistrate Wang Xifan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once his request was granted, he recommended Shandong grain intendant Chi Rixun, Henan grain intendant Fan Zhou, Wuxi magistrate Wu Xingzuo, and others, and impeached Liyang magistrate Wang Xifan and others.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吳三桂兵犯江西，十月，命帥顏保帥所部移鎮南昌。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wu Sangui's troops invaded Jiangxi; in the tenth month Shuaibao was ordered to lead his command to garrison Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Wu Sangui's forces invaded Jiangxi; in the tenth month Shuaibao was ordered to move his command to garrison Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，安親王岳樂師至，命罷還。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Prince An Yuele's army arrived and he was ordered to stand down and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince An Yuele's army arrived and he was ordered to stand down and return.

sentences.zh: 十七年，岳樂進軍湖南，復命鎮南昌。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yuele advanced into Hunan and he was again ordered to garrison Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yuele marched into Hunan and Shuaibao was again ordered to garrison Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，移吉安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he moved to Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he moved his headquarters to Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 十八年三月，招降吳三桂部將五十餘、兵萬餘。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighteenth year he induced more than fifty of Wu Sangui's generals and more than ten thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighteenth year he induced more than fifty of Wu Sangui's generals and more than ten thousand troops to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，逮尚之信勘治，命帥顏保移鎮南雄、韶州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year Shang Zhixin was arrested for investigation; Shuaibao was ordered to move his garrison to Nanxiong and Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year Shang Zhixin was arrested for investigation; Shuaibao was ordered to garrison Nanxiong and Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，命罷還。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to stand down and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to stand down and return.

sentences.zh: 二十年五月，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year he was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 十二月，移禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was transferred to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the twenty-third year.

sentences.zh: 子赫奕，自侍衛累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Heyi rose from bodyguard through successive promotions to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heyi rose from the imperial guard through successive promotions to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 嵩壽，希福曾孫。

translations.literal: Songsou, Xi Fu's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Songsou was Xi Fu's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the first year of Yongzheng, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed revising compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Yongzheng, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed revising compiler.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，冊封安南國王黎維禕，以侍讀充正使，賜一品服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, when investiture was conferred on the king of Annam, Le Duy Vi, he served as chief envoy in the capacity of reader-in-waiting and was granted first-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong, when the investiture of the king of Annam, Le Duy Vi, was performed, he served as chief envoy in the capacity of reader-in-waiting and was granted first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十四年，頒詔朝鮮，擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he proclaimed an edict in Korea and was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he proclaimed an edict in Korea and was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，襲一等子爵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he inherited the first-rank zi peerage.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he inherited the first-rank zi peerage.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 范文程，字憲鬥，宋觀文殿大學士高平公純仁十七世孫也。

translations.literal: Fan Wencheng, style Xiandou, was the seventeenth-generation descendant of the Song Guanwen Hall Grand Secretary and Duke of Gaoping, Fan Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wencheng, style Xiandou, was the seventeenth-generation descendant of the Song Guanwen Hall grand secretary and Duke of Gaoping, Fan Chunren.

sentences.zh: 其先世，明初自江西謫瀋陽，遂為瀋陽人，居撫順所。

translations.literal: His ancestors, in the early Ming, were banished from Jiangxi to Shenyang and thus became Shenyang natives, dwelling at Fushun garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had been banished from Jiangxi to Shenyang in the early Ming and thus became Shenyang natives, living at Fushun garrison.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鏓，正德間進士，官至兵部尚書，明史有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Juan was a jinshi in the Zhengde reign and rose to Minister of War; he has a biography in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Juan was a jinshi in the Zhengde reign, rose to minister of war, and has a biography in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 文程少好讀書，穎敏沈毅，與其兄文寀並為瀋陽縣學生員。

translations.literal: Wencheng from youth loved reading; he was quick-witted, steady, and resolute, and he and his elder brother Wencai were both licentiates of Shenyang county school.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wencheng loved books; he was quick-witted, steady, and resolute, and he and his elder brother Wencai were both licentiates of the Shenyang county school.

sentences.zh: 天命三年，太祖既下撫順，文寀、文程共謁太祖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianming, after the Grand Ancestor had taken Fushun, Wencai and Wencheng together paid their respects to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianming, after the Taizu Emperor had taken Fushun, Wencai and Wencheng together presented themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 太祖偉文程，與語，器之，知為鏓曾孫，顧謂諸貝勒曰：「此名臣後也，善遇之！」

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor thought Wencheng imposing; he spoke with him, valued him, learned that he was Juan's great-grandson, and turning to the beile said: "This is the descendant of a famous minister—treat him well!"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor was struck by Wencheng's bearing; he spoke with him, took him in favor, learned that he was Juan's great-grandson, and turning to the princes said: "This is the descendant of a famous minister—treat him well!"

sentences.zh: 上伐明，取遼陽，度三岔攻西平，下廣寧，文程皆在行間。

translations.literal: When the sovereign campaigned against the Ming, took Liaoyang, crossed at Sancha to attack Xiping, and captured Guangning, Wencheng was in the ranks on every campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against the Ming, took Liaoyang, crossed at Sancha to attack Xiping, and captured Guangning, Wencheng was with the army throughout.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，召直左右。

translations.literal: When the Taizong Emperor acceded, he was summoned to attend at the sovereign's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji acceded, Wencheng was summoned to attend at his side.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，復從伐明，入薊門，克遵化。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he again followed the campaign against the Ming, entered Jimen, and captured Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancong he again joined the campaign against the Ming, entered Jimen, and captured Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 文程別將偏師徇潘家口、馬蘭峪、三屯營、馬欄關、大安口，凡五城皆下。

translations.literal: Wencheng separately commanded a detached force to subdue Panjiakou, Malanyu, Santunying, Malanguan, and Da'ankou—five cities in all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng led a detached force against Panjiakou, Malanyu, Santunying, Malanguan, and Da'ankou—all five places fell.

sentences.zh: 既，明圍我師大安口，文程以火器進攻，圍解。

translations.literal: Afterward the Ming besieged our army at Da'ankou; Wencheng attacked with firearms and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ming forces besieged the army at Da'ankou; Wencheng attacked with firearms and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 太宗自將略永平，留文程守遵化，敵掩至，文程率先力戰，敵敗走。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor personally led a thrust toward Yongping and left Wencheng to hold Zunhua; the enemy made a surprise attack, Wencheng led the charge and fought hard, and the enemy was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji personally led a thrust toward Yongping and left Wencheng to hold Zunhua; when the enemy struck by surprise, Wencheng led the charge, fought fiercely, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 以功授世職游擊。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the hereditary rank of Guerrilla Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was granted the hereditary rank of guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 五年，師圍大凌河，降其城，而蒙古降卒有陰戕其將叛去者，上怒甚，文程從容進說，貸死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the army besieged Dalinghe and the city surrendered; but among the Mongol surrendered troops some had secretly killed their officers and rebelled. The sovereign was greatly angered; Wencheng calmly remonstrated and more than five hundred condemned to death were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the army besieged Dalinghe and the city surrendered; but some Mongol surrendered troops had secretly killed their officers and rebelled. The emperor was furious; Wencheng calmly remonstrated and more than five hundred men condemned to death were spared.

sentences.zh: 時明別將壁西山之巔，獨負險堅守未下，文程單騎抵其壘，諭以利害，乃請降。

translations.literal: At that time a Ming detached general held the crest of West Mountain, alone relying on the terrain and holding out; Wencheng rode alone to his camp, explained advantage and harm, and he then asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming detached general still held the crest of West Mountain, relying on the terrain; Wencheng rode alone to his camp, explained the stakes, and the general then asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上悅，以降人盡賜文程。

translations.literal: The sovereign was pleased and gave all the surrendered men to Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and gave all the surrendered men to Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 六年，從上略明邊，文程與同直文館寧完我、馬國柱上疏論兵事，以為入宣、大，不若攻山海。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the sovereign in raiding the Ming frontier; Wencheng, together with his colleagues in the Literary Bureau Ning Wanwo and Ma Guozhu, memorialized on military affairs, holding that entering Xuan and Da was inferior to attacking Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the raid on the Ming frontier; Wencheng, together with his Literary Bureau colleagues Ning Wanwo and Ma Guozhu, memorialized on military affairs, arguing that penetrating Xuan and Da was inferior to striking Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 及師至歸化城，上策深入，召文程等與謀。

translations.literal: When the army reached Guihua city, the sovereign planned a deep thrust and summoned Wencheng and the others to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Guihua, the emperor planned a deep thrust and summoned Wencheng and the others to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 文程等疏言：「察我軍情狀，志皆在深入。

translations.literal: Wencheng and the others memorialized: "Observing the mood of our army, all wish to press deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng and the others memorialized: "Judging the mood of our troops, every man wishes to press deep.

sentences.zh: 當直抵北京決和否，毀山海關水門而歸，以張軍威。

translations.literal: We should strike straight for Beijing to settle peace or war, destroy the water gates of Shanhai Pass on the return, and thereby display our military might.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike straight for Beijing to settle peace or war, break the water gates of Shanhai Pass on the return, and thereby display our military might.

sentences.zh: 若計所從入，惟雁門為便，道既無阻，道旁居民富庶，可資以為糧。

translations.literal: If we consider the route of entry, only Yanmen is convenient—the road is unobstructed and the inhabitants along the way are prosperous, so we may draw provisions from them.
translations.idiomatic: Of the routes inward, only Yanmen is convenient—the road is clear and the inhabitants along the way are prosperous enough to supply our grain.

sentences.zh: 上如慮師無名，當顯諭其民，言察哈爾汗遠遁，所部歸於我，道遠不可以徒行，來與爾國議和，假爾馬以濟我新附之眾。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty fears the army lacks a pretext, you should openly announce to their people that the Chahar khan has fled far away, his tribes have submitted to us, the road is too long to travel on foot, we have come to negotiate peace with your state, and we ask to borrow your horses to convey our newly submitted masses.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty fears the campaign lacks a pretext, you should openly announce to their people that the Chahar khan has fled, his tribes have submitted to us, the road is too long to march on foot, we have come to negotiate peace with your state, and we ask to borrow your horses to convey our newly submitted followers.

sentences.zh: 和議成，償馬值；

translations.literal: If peace is concluded, compensate the value of the horses;
translations.idiomatic: If peace is concluded, compensate the value of the horses;

sentences.zh: 不成，異日興師，荷天之寵，以版圖歸我，凡軍興而擾及者，當量免賦稅數年。

translations.literal: if not, when we raise the army on another day and, favored by Heaven, bring their territory under our rule, all whom military action has disturbed should have their taxes remitted for several years according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: if not, when we raise the army again and, favored by Heaven, bring their territory under our rule, all whom military action has disturbed should have their taxes remitted for several years as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 此所謂堂堂正正之師也。

translations.literal: This is what is called a grand and righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by a grand and righteous campaign.

sentences.zh: 否則，作書抵近邊諸將吏，使以議和請於其主，為期決進止。

translations.literal: Otherwise, write to the frontier generals and officials, have them request peace negotiations from their sovereign, and set a deadline to decide advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, write to the frontier generals and officials, have them request peace negotiations from their sovereign, and set a deadline for a decision.

sentences.zh: 彼朝臣內撓，邊將外諉，遷延逾所期，我師即乘釁而入。

translations.literal: Their courtiers will quarrel within, frontier generals will shift blame without, and delay will pass the deadline—then our army may seize the opening and enter.
translations.idiomatic: Their courtiers will quarrel within, frontier generals will shift blame without, and delay will pass the deadline—then our army may seize the opening and strike.

sentences.zh: 我師進，利在深入；

translations.literal: When our army advances, the advantage lies in pressing deep;
translations.idiomatic: When our army advances, the advantage lies in pressing deep;

sentences.zh: 否，利在速歸；

translations.literal: if not, the advantage lies in swift return;
translations.idiomatic: if not, the advantage lies in a swift return;

sentences.zh: 半途而返，無益也。」

translations.literal: to turn back halfway is of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: to turn back halfway gains nothing."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上深嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the sovereign deeply praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor warmly approved it.

sentences.zh: 七年，孔有德等使通款，而明兵迫之急，上命文程從諸貝勒帥師赴援；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Kong Youde and others sent envoys to negotiate terms, but Ming forces pressed them hard; the sovereign ordered Wencheng to follow the beile in commanding troops to relieve them;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Kong Youde and others opened negotiations, but Ming forces pressed them hard; the emperor ordered Wencheng to accompany the princes in leading troops to their relief;

sentences.zh: 文程宣上德意，有德等遂以所部來歸。

translations.literal: Wencheng proclaimed the sovereign's gracious intent, and Youde and the others then brought their followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng proclaimed the emperor's gracious intent, and Youde and his followers then submitted with their troops.

sentences.zh: 自是破旅順，收平島，討朝鮮，撫定蒙古，文程皆與謀。

translations.literal: From then on, in breaking Lüshun, recovering Ping Island, campaigning against Korea, and pacifying the Mongols, Wencheng took part in the deliberations on every occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whether in taking Lüshun, recovering Ping Island, campaigning against Korea, or pacifying the Mongols, Wencheng was consulted on every major decision.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，改文館為內三院，以文程為內秘書院大學士，進世職二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, the Literary Institute was changed to the Inner Three Courts; Wencheng was made grand secretary of the Inner Secretariat Court and advanced in hereditary rank to second-class jalan-i janggū.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde the Literary Institute became the Inner Three Courts; Wencheng was appointed grand secretary of the Inner Secretariat Court and advanced in hereditary rank to second-class jalan-i janggū.

sentences.zh: 初，旗制既定，設固山額真。

translations.literal: At first, once the banner system was fixed, gūsa i ejen were established.
translations.idiomatic: When the banner system was first fixed, banner commanders were established.

sentences.zh: 諸臣議首推文程，上曰：「范章京才誠勝此，然固山職一軍耳，朕方資為心膂。

translations.literal: The ministers deliberated and wished to nominate Wencheng first; the sovereign said: "Secretary Fan's talent truly surpasses this post, yet the gūsa office commands only one army; I am now employing him as my heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wished to nominate Wencheng first; the emperor said: "Secretary Fan's talent truly surpasses this post, yet a banner command commands only one army; I am now relying on him as my right hand.

sentences.zh: 其別議之。」

translations.literal: Discuss another candidate."
translations.idiomatic: Nominate someone else."

sentences.zh: 文程所典皆機密事，每入對，必漏下數十刻始出；

translations.literal: Wencheng handled matters all of a confidential nature; each time he entered audience, several tens of kè would pass the water clock before he came out;
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng handled confidential affairs; each audience lasted many hours before he emerged;

sentences.zh: 或未及食息，復召入。

translations.literal: sometimes before he had eaten or rested, he was summoned in again.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes he was summoned back before he had eaten or rested.

sentences.zh: 上重文程，每議政，必曰：「范章京知否？」

translations.literal: The sovereign valued Wencheng highly; whenever state affairs were discussed, he would always say: "Does Secretary Fan know of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Wencheng highly; whenever policy was discussed, he would ask: "Has Secretary Fan been told?"

sentences.zh: 脫有未當，曰：「何不與范章京議之？」

translations.literal: If something seemed improper, he would say: "Why not discuss it with Secretary Fan?"
translations.idiomatic: If something seemed amiss, he would say: "Why not consult Secretary Fan?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「范亦云爾。」

translations.literal: The assembly would say: "Fan says the same.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers would reply: "Fan agrees."

sentences.zh: 上輒署可。

translations.literal: The sovereign would then mark it approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would then approve it.

sentences.zh: 文程嘗以疾在告，庶務填委，命待范章京病已裁決。

translations.literal: Wencheng once reported ill; miscellaneous affairs piled up, and the order was to await Secretary Fan's recovery before deciding them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng once reported ill, routine business piled up and orders were held until Secretary Fan recovered to decide them.

sentences.zh: 撫諭各國書敕，皆文程視草。

translations.literal: Letters and edicts comforting and instructing the various states were all drafted under Wencheng's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: All letters and edicts comforting and instructing the various states were drafted under Wencheng's supervision.

sentences.zh: 初，上猶省覽，後乃不復詳審，曰：「汝當無謬也。」

translations.literal: At first the sovereign still reviewed them; afterward he no longer examined them in detail and said: "You surely make no error."
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor still reviewed them; later he ceased to examine them closely and said: "You will make no mistake."

sentences.zh: 文程迎父楠侍養，嘗入侍上食，有珍味，文程私念父所未嘗，逡巡不下箸。

translations.literal: Wencheng received his father Nan to attend and support him; he once entered to attend the sovereign at a meal; there was a rare delicacy; Wencheng privately thought his father had never tasted it and hesitated, not lowering his chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng brought his father Nan home to care for him; once, while attending the emperor at a meal, he saw a rare delicacy and, thinking his father had never tasted it, hesitated and did not eat.

sentences.zh: 上察其意，即命徹饌以賜楠，文程再拜謝。

translations.literal: The sovereign perceived his meaning and immediately ordered the dish withdrawn to be bestowed on Nan; Wencheng bowed twice in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and immediately had the dish sent to Nan; Wencheng bowed twice in thanks.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，命隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was ordered to be registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor acceded, Wencheng was registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞帥師伐明，文程上書言：「中原百姓蹇離喪亂，備極荼毒，思擇令主，以圖樂業。

translations.literal: Prince Regent Dorgon led the army against the Ming; Wencheng submitted a memorial saying: "The people of the Central Plains, scattered and ruined in disorder, have suffered every extremity of misery and long to choose a worthy ruler so as to seek secure livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Regent Dorgon led the army against the Ming, Wencheng wrote: "The people of the Central Plains, scattered in war and ruin, have suffered every misery and long for a worthy ruler under whom they may live in peace.

sentences.zh: 曩者棄遵化，屠永平，兩次深入而復返。

translations.literal: Formerly we abandoned Zunhua, slaughtered at Yongping, and twice advanced deep only to return.
translations.idiomatic: We once abandoned Zunhua, slaughtered at Yongping, and twice marched deep into their territory only to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 彼必以我為無大志，惟金帛子女是圖，因懷疑貳。

translations.literal: They must take us as lacking great ambition, caring only for gold, silk, women, and children, and so harbor doubt and divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: They must believe we lack great ambition and care only for gold, silk, and captives, and so they doubt and waver.

sentences.zh: 今當申嚴紀律，秋毫勿犯，宣諭進取中原之意：官仍其職，民復其業，錄賢能，卹無告。

translations.literal: Now we should strictly enforce discipline, violating not a hair's breadth, and proclaim our intent to advance into the Central Plains: officials keep their posts, the people resume their occupations, the worthy are recorded, the helpless are relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Now we must enforce strict discipline and harm nothing; proclaim our intent to take the Central Plains—officials shall keep their posts, the people their livelihoods, the worthy shall be employed, the helpless relieved.

sentences.zh: 大河以北，可傳檄定也。」

translations.literal: North of the Great River, territories may be settled by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: North of the Great River, the land may be won by proclamation alone."

sentences.zh: 及流賊李自成破明都，報至，文程方養疴蓋州湯泉，驛召決策，文程曰：「闖寇塗炭中原，戕厥君後，此必討之賊也。

translations.literal: When the bandit Li Zicheng broke the Ming capital and the report arrived, Wencheng was recuperating at Gaizhou's Tangquan hot springs; an express summons called him to decide policy. Wencheng said: "The Dashing Bandit has charred the Central Plains and killed the ruler's house—this is an enemy who must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng's rebels took the Ming capital and word arrived, Wencheng was convalescing at Gaizhou's Tangquan springs; an express summons brought him to counsel. He said: "The Dashing Bandit has ravaged the Central Plains and killed the imperial house—he is an enemy who must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 雖擁眾百萬，橫行無憚，其敗道有三：逼殞其主，天怒矣；

translations.literal: Though he commands millions and rampages without fear, there are three ways to his defeat: forcing the ruler to his death—Heaven is enraged;
translations.idiomatic: Though he commands a million men and rampages without restraint, three paths lead to his defeat: he forced the emperor to his death—Heaven is enraged;

sentences.zh: 刑辱搢紳，拷劫財貨，士忿矣；

translations.literal: punishing and humiliating the gentry, torturing and plundering wealth—the scholar-officials are furious;
translations.idiomatic: he tortured and humiliated the gentry and extorted their wealth—the scholar-officials are furious;

sentences.zh: 掠人貲，淫人婦，火人廬舍，民恨矣。

translations.literal: seizing people's goods, violating people's wives, burning people's homes—the people hate him.
translations.idiomatic: he seized goods, violated women, and burned homes—the people hate him.

sentences.zh: 備此三敗，行之以驕，可一戰破也。

translations.literal: With these three causes of defeat in place and arrogance added to his conduct, he may be broken in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: With these three defeats prepared and arrogance in his conduct, he can be broken in one battle.

sentences.zh: 我國上下同心，兵甲選練，聲罪以臨之，卹其士夫，拯其黎庶。

translations.literal: Our state is united above and below, arms and armor are select and trained; proclaim his crimes and march against him, comfort his scholar-officials, and rescue his common people.
translations.idiomatic: Our state is united, our arms are honed; proclaim his crimes, march against him, comfort his gentry, and rescue his people.

sentences.zh: 兵以義動，何功不成？」

translations.literal: An army moved by righteousness—what achievement could fail?"
translations.idiomatic: An army that fights in the name of justice—what can it not accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「好生者天之德也，古未有嗜殺而得天下者。

translations.literal: He also said: "Loving life is Heaven's virtue; antiquity never saw one who delighted in killing yet gained the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Cherishing life is Heaven's virtue; never in antiquity did one who delighted in slaughter gain the realm.

sentences.zh: 國家止欲帝關東則已，若將統一區夏，非乂安百姓不可。」

translations.literal: If the state only wishes to rule as emperor east of the Pass, so be it; but if it will unify all within the Four Seas, it cannot be done without governing and securing the people."
translations.idiomatic: If the state only wishes to rule east of the Pass, so be it; but to unify the realm, the people must be governed and secured."

sentences.zh: 翌日，馳赴軍中草檄，諭明吏民言：「義師為爾复君父仇，非殺爾百姓，今所誅者惟闖賊。

translations.literal: The next day he galloped to the army and drafted a proclamation, instructing Ming officials and people: "The righteous army comes to avenge your ruler and father for you—not to kill you, the common people; those who will be executed now are only the Dashing Bandit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he rode to the army and drafted a proclamation to Ming officials and people: "This righteous army comes to avenge your ruler and father, not to kill the people; only the Dashing Bandit will be punished.

sentences.zh: 吏來歸，復其位；

translations.literal: Officials who come in submission shall have their posts restored;
translations.idiomatic: Officials who submit shall have their posts restored;

sentences.zh: 民來歸，復其業。

translations.literal: people who come in submission shall have their livelihoods restored.
translations.idiomatic: the people who submit shall resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 師行以律，必不汝害。」

translations.literal: The army marches by discipline and assuredly will not harm you."
translations.idiomatic: The army marches under strict discipline and will not harm you."

sentences.zh: 檄皆署文程官階、姓氏。

translations.literal: The proclamations all bore Wencheng's official rank and surname.
translations.idiomatic: Every proclamation bore Wencheng's rank and name.

sentences.zh: 既克明都，百度草創，用文程議，為明莊烈愍皇帝發喪，安撫孑遺，舉用廢官，蒐求隱逸，甄考文獻，更定律令，廣開言路，招集諸曹胥吏，徵求冊籍。

translations.literal: After the Ming capital was taken, a hundred affairs were in first creation; following Wencheng's counsel, they held funeral rites for the Ming Zhuanglie Min Emperor, comforted the survivors, employed dismissed officials, sought out recluses, examined documents, revised laws and ordinances, opened the way for remonstrance, gathered clerks of the various bureaus, and sought registers and records.
translations.idiomatic: After Beijing fell and government was being built anew, they followed Wencheng's advice: funeral rites for the Chongzhen Emperor, relief for survivors, reinstatement of dismissed officials, search for recluses, review of records, revision of laws, opening of channels for remonstrance, recall of bureau clerks, and collection of registers.

sentences.zh: 明季賦額屢加，冊皆毀於寇，惟萬曆時故籍存，或欲下直省求新冊，文程曰：「即此為額，猶慮病民，其可更求乎？」

translations.literal: Late-Ming tax quotas were repeatedly raised, and the registers were destroyed by the bandits; only the old registers from the Wanli reign survived. Some wished to order the provinces to seek new registers. Wencheng said: "Even using these as the quota still fears burdening the people—how could we seek more?"
translations.idiomatic: Late-Ming tax quotas had been raised repeatedly, and the registers were destroyed in the turmoil; only Wanli-era records survived. Some proposed ordering the provinces to compile new registers. Wencheng said: "Even these old quotas may burden the people—how can we seek more?"

sentences.zh: 於是議遂定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 論功，並遇恩詔，進一等阿思哈尼哈番加拖沙喇哈番，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, he also met with an amnesty edict and was advanced one grade to ashan i hafan plus toosyaha hafan, and granted the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: For his service he also received an amnesty promotion to ashan i hafan with toosyaha hafan and the title "Bakshi."

sentences.zh: 復進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to second-class jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He was further advanced to second-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，江南既定，文程上疏言：「治天下在得民心，士為秀民。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, after the south of the Yangzi was settled, Wencheng submitted a memorial saying: "Governing the realm lies in winning the people's hearts; the gentry are the outstanding among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year two, after the lower Yangzi was pacified, Wencheng memorialized: "To govern the realm one must win hearts; the gentry are the leading people.

sentences.zh: 士心得，則民心得矣。

translations.literal: When the gentry's hearts are won, the people's hearts are won.
translations.idiomatic: Win the gentry and you win the people.

sentences.zh: 請再行鄉、會試，廣其登進。」

translations.literal: He asked that provincial and metropolitan examinations be held again and advancement broadened."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that provincial and metropolitan examinations be restored and advancement broadened."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，定內三院為文臣班首，命文程及剛林、祁充格用珠頂、玉帶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, the Inner Three Courts were fixed as head of the civil official order; Wencheng and Ganglin and Qi Chongge were ordered to use pearl finials and jade belts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five the Inner Three Courts were made chief among civil officials; Wencheng, Ganglin, and Qi Chongge were granted pearl finials and jade belts.

sentences.zh: 七年，睿親王多爾袞卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Prince Regent Dorgon died.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Prince Regent Dorgon died.

sentences.zh: 八年，大學士剛林、祁充格以附睿親王妄改太祖實錄，坐死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, grand secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge, for following the Prince Regent in falsely altering the Taizu Veritable Records, were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were executed for following the Prince Regent in falsifying the Taizu Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 文程與同官當連坐，上以文程不附睿親王，命但奪官論贖。

translations.literal: Wencheng and his colleagues should have been implicated, but because the sovereign found Wencheng had not sided with the Prince Regent, he ordered only deprivation of office with redemption by fine.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng should have been implicated, but because he had not sided with the Prince Regent, the emperor ordered only removal from office with a fine in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 是歲即復官。

translations.literal: That same year his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: That year his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 九年，遇恩詔，復進世職一等精奇尼哈番，授議政大臣，監修太宗實錄。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, meeting an amnesty edict, he was again advanced in hereditary rank to first-class jingkini hafan, appointed deliberating minister, and charged to supervise compilation of the Taizong Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, on an amnesty, he was advanced to first-class jingkini hafan, appointed deliberating minister, and charged to supervise the Taizong Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 時直省錢糧多不如額，一歲至缺四百餘萬，賦虧餉絀。

translations.literal: At that time grain and money levies in the provinces often fell short of quota; in one year the shortfall reached more than four million, and with taxes deficient, pay was in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial grain and tax revenues often fell short; in one year the deficit exceeded four million taels, leaving pay in arrears.

sentences.zh: 文程疏言：「湖廣、江西、河南、山東、陝西五省亂久民稀，請興屯，設道二、同知四，令督撫選屬吏廉能敏幹者任之，以選吏當否為督撫功罪。

translations.literal: Wencheng submitted a memorial saying: "Huguang, Jiangxi, Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi—the five provinces long disturbed and sparsely peopled—should undertake military colonies; establish two circuit intendants and four sub-prefects, and have governors and governors-general select subordinates who are honest, capable, and diligent to fill them, making the choice of officials the measure of the governors' merit or fault.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng memorialized: "In Huguang, Jiangxi, Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi—provinces long ravaged and thinly settled—establish military colonies: two circuit intendants and four sub-prefects, with governors selecting honest, capable men, and judging governors by the quality of those appointments.

sentences.zh: 官吏俸廩，初年出興屯母財，次年以所穫償。

translations.literal: Officials' salaries and rations: in the first year drawn from the colony's founding capital; in the second year repaid from the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries: in the first year paid from colony seed funds; in the second year repaid from the harvest.

sentences.zh: 自後皆出所穫，官增而俸不費。

translations.literal: Afterward all came from the harvest; offices increased while salaries cost the treasury nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all came from the harvest—more officials without burdening the treasury.

sentences.zh: 屯用牛，若穀種，若農器，聽興屯道發州縣倉庫以具。

translations.literal: For colonies, oxen, grain seed, and farm tools—let the colony intendant issue them from prefectural and county storehouses as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen, seed grain, and farm tools for the colonies should be issued from prefectural and county storehouses on the intendant's order.

sentences.zh: 屯始駐兵，地荒蕪多而水道便者，以次及其餘。

translations.literal: At first troops were stationed on the colonies; among lands much waste but with convenient waterways, take those first, then the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At first troops would garrison the colonies; prioritize waste land with good water access, then the remainder.

sentences.zh: 地無主，若有主而棄不耕，皆為官屯。

translations.literal: Land without owners, or with owners who abandoned cultivation, all became official colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Ownerless land, or land owners had abandoned, became official colonies.

sentences.zh: 民原耕而財不足，官佐以牛若穀種，分所穫三之一，三年後為民業。

translations.literal: Where the people wished to farm but lacked means, the state aided with oxen or seed grain and took one-third of the harvest; after three years it became the people's property.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants who wished to farm but lacked means would receive oxen or seed; one-third of the harvest went to the state; after three years the land became theirs.

sentences.zh: 編保甲，使助守望，絕姦宄。

translations.literal: Organize baojia so they aid watch and ward and cut off evil-doers.
translations.idiomatic: Organize baojia for mutual watch and to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 若無財，官畀以傭值。

translations.literal: If they lacked means, officials should provide wages.
translations.idiomatic: Those without means should receive wages from the government.

sentences.zh: 民將逭飢，流亡當大集。

translations.literal: When the people were about to escape famine, refugees would gather in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: As famine threatened, refugees would gather in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 初年所穫糧草，聽屯吏儲留，出陳易新，為次年母財；

translations.literal: Grain and fodder of the first year's harvest might be stored by colony officials, old stock exchanged for new, serving as the next year's founding capital;
translations.idiomatic: First-year grain and fodder could be stored by colony officials, rotated stock for new, and used as seed capital the next year;

sentences.zh: 有餘，畀近屯駐軍，勿為額以取盈。

translations.literal: if there was surplus, give it to nearby garrison troops; do not treat quotas as a pretext for surplus-taking.
translations.idiomatic: surplus could supply nearby garrisons—without using quotas as an excuse to extract more.

sentences.zh: 三年所穫浸多，僦舟車運以饋餉。

translations.literal: In the third year, as harvests gradually increased, hire boats and carts to transport provisions for pay.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year, as harvests grew, hire transport to deliver provisions for army pay.

sentences.zh: 毋煩屯吏，毋役屯民，毋用屯牛。

translations.literal: Do not trouble colony officials, do not conscript colony people, do not use colony oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Colony officials, peasants, and oxen should not be conscripted for transport.

sentences.zh: 屯所在州縣吏受興屯道​​指揮，屯吏稱其職，三歲進二秩，視邊俸；

translations.literal: County and prefectural officials where colonies lay received orders from the colony intendant; colony officials who performed their duties were advanced two ranks after three years, with frontier-level salaries;
translations.idiomatic: Local officials in colony districts would answer to the intendant; diligent colony officers would advance two ranks after three years at frontier pay;

sentences.zh: 不職，責撫按糾舉；

translations.literal: if they did not perform, governors and governors-general were to impeach;
translations.idiomatic: the incompetent would be impeached by governors;

sentences.zh: 有所徇，則並坐：所謂信賞必罰也。」

translations.literal: if there was favoritism, all would be punished together—this is what is called certain reward and certain punishment."
translations.idiomatic: favoritism would be punished together—true reward and true punishment."

sentences.zh: 上深韙其議。

translations.literal: The sovereign deeply approved his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 十年，復與同官疏：「請敕部院三品以上大臣，各舉所知，毋問滿、漢新舊，毋泥官秩高下，毋避親疏恩怨，舉惟其才，各具專疏，臚舉實跡，置御前以時召對。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again memorialized with his colleagues: "We ask that ministers of the third rank and above in the ministries and courts each recommend those they know, without regard to Manchu, Han, new or old, without being bound by official rank high or low, without avoiding kinship, distance, or old grievances—recommend only by talent, each in a separate memorial setting forth verified facts, placed before the throne for timely audience.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Let ministers of the third rank and above in every ministry recommend those they know—Manchu or Han, new or old, high or low rank, kin or foe—on merit alone, each in a separate memorial with verified facts, for timely audience before the throne.

sentences.zh: 察其論議，覈其行事，並視其舉主為何如人，則其人堪任與否，上早所深鑑，待缺簡用。

translations.literal: Observe their discourse, verify their conduct, and also see what sort of man their recommender is; then whether the candidate is fit for office, the sovereign will early have deep insight and appoint when a vacancy opens.
translations.idiomatic: Judge their speech and deeds, and note who recommended them; the emperor will know early whether they are fit and appoint them when posts open.

sentences.zh: 稱職，量效之大小，舉主同其賞；

translations.literal: If they perform their duties, measure the effect great or small and the recommender shares the reward;
translations.idiomatic: If they succeed, reward them in proportion—and reward the recommender likewise;

sentences.zh: 不稱職，​​量罪之大小，舉主同其罰。」

translations.literal: if they do not perform, measure the offense great or small and the recommender shares the punishment."
translations.idiomatic: if they fail, punish in proportion—and punish the recommender likewise."

sentences.zh: 上特允所請。

translations.literal: The sovereign specially granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 上勤於政治，屢幸內院，進諸臣從容諮訪。

translations.literal: The sovereign was diligent in government and repeatedly visited the Inner Court, advancing the ministers to consult at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was diligent in government, often visiting the Inner Court to consult his ministers at leisure.

sentences.zh: 文程每以班首承旨，陳對稱上意。

translations.literal: Wencheng, as head of the civil order, received the edict and replied in a manner that matched the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng, as senior minister, received his instructions and answered to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 嘗值端陽，諸臣散直差早，上曰：「乘藉天休，猥圖安樂，人情盡然。

translations.literal: Once on the Dragon Boat Festival the ministers were dismissed from duty rather early; the sovereign said: "Taking advantage of Heaven's rest, we meanly seek ease and pleasure—human feeling is entirely so.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Dragon Boat Festival the ministers left early; the emperor said: "Heaven grants rest and we seek ease—such is human nature.

sentences.zh: 特欲逸必先勞，俾國家大定，其樂方永。

translations.literal: Yet if one wishes leisure, one must first labor; only when the state is greatly settled will joy be lasting.
translations.idiomatic: But leisure must follow labor; only when the realm is secure will joy endure.

sentences.zh: 不然，樂亦暫耳。」

translations.literal: Otherwise joy is but momentary."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise pleasure is fleeting."

sentences.zh: 復言：「人孰無過，能改之為美。

translations.literal: He went on: "Who among men is without fault? To be able to reform is beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "Who is without fault? The beauty lies in reform.

sentences.zh: 成湯盛德，改過不吝。

translations.literal: King Tang's great virtue lay in not grudging to correct his faults.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang's greatness was his willingness to correct his faults.

sentences.zh: 若明武宗嬉遊無度，諉罪於其臣，豈修己治人之道耶？」

translations.literal: But when the Ming Wuzong indulged in pleasure without measure and shifted blame to his ministers—was that the way to cultivate oneself and govern others?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming Wuzong played without restraint and blamed his ministers—was that how a ruler cultivates himself and governs others?"

sentences.zh: 文程因奏：「君明臣良，必交勉釋回，始克荷天休，濟國事。」

translations.literal: Wencheng thereupon memorialized: "When the ruler is enlightened and the minister worthy, they must encourage each other and release doubt—only then can they bear Heaven's favor and carry out state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng replied: "When ruler and minister are both worthy, they must encourage each other—only then can they enjoy Heaven's favor and serve the state."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Well said.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，朕有過即改。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever I have a fault I shall reform it.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever I err I shall correct it.

sentences.zh: 卿等亦宜黽勉，毋忘啟沃可也！」

translations.literal: You ministers too should strive diligently; do not forget to counsel and assist!"
translations.idiomatic: You too must strive—do not fail to counsel me!"

sentences.zh: 上嘗命遣官蒞各省卹刑，文程言：「前此遣滿、漢大臣巡方，慮擾民，故罷。

translations.literal: The sovereign once ordered officials sent to the provinces to review punishments with compassion; Wencheng said: "Previously Manchu and Han grand ministers were sent to tour the regions, but for fear of disturbing the people this was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered officials sent to the provinces to review punishments; Wencheng said: "Earlier tours by Manchu and Han grand ministers disturbed the people and were stopped.

sentences.zh: 今四方水旱災傷，民勞未息，宜罷遣使。

translations.literal: Now in the four quarters flood, drought, and disaster wounds afflict the people; labor has not yet ceased—it is fitting to stop sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Now floods, droughts, and disasters afflict every region and the people are not yet at rest—envoys should not be sent.

sentences.zh: 現禁重囚，令各省巡撫詳勘，有可矜疑，奏聞裁定。」

translations.literal: Heavy criminals are now forbidden; let each province's governor-general examine in detail, and where there is ground for mercy or doubt, memorialize for the throne to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy criminals are already restricted; let each governor examine cases and memorialize where mercy or doubt applies."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The sovereign adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 文程論政，務簡耍，持大體，多類是。

translations.literal: When Wencheng discussed government, he aimed at what was essential and brief, held to the great pattern, and mostly resembled this.
translations.idiomatic: In policy Wencheng favored what was essential and brief, held to the larger pattern, and mostly counseled in this vein.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，上加恩輔政諸臣，特加文程少保兼太子太保，文程疏謝，因自陳衰病，乞休。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year, when the sovereign added favor to assisting ministers, he specially advanced Wencheng to Junior Guardian and concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Wencheng submitted thanks and, declaring his age and illness, begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year eleven the emperor honored his assisting ministers and advanced Wencheng to Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Wencheng thanked him and, citing age and illness, asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 九月，上降溫諭，進太傅兼太子太師，致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the sovereign issued a warm edict, advancing him to Grand Tutor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor issued a gracious edict, advanced him to Grand Tutor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 上以文程祖宗朝舊臣，有大功於國家，禮遇甚厚：文程疾，嘗親調藥餌以賜；

translations.literal: Because Wencheng was an old minister from the dynastic founders and had great merit for the state, the favor shown him was very thick: when Wencheng was ill, the sovereign would personally compound medicines and bestow them;
translations.idiomatic: As a founding minister of great service, he was treated with exceptional honor: when ill, the emperor personally prepared medicine for him;

sentences.zh: 遣畫工就第圖其像，藏之內府；

translations.literal: he sent painters to his residence to paint his portrait and stored it in the inner treasury;
translations.idiomatic: sent painters to his home to paint his portrait for the inner treasury;

sentences.zh: 賚御用服物，多不勝紀；

translations.literal: he bestowed imperial garments and objects beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: and bestowed imperial robes and gifts beyond number;

sentences.zh: 又以文程形貌頎偉，命特製衣冠，求其稱體。

translations.literal: Again, because Wencheng's stature was tall and imposing, the sovereign ordered garments and caps specially made to fit him properly.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wencheng was tall and imposing, the emperor also had robes and caps custom-made to fit him well.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，特命祭告太宗山陵，伏地哀慟不能起。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor acceded, he specially ordered Wencheng to offer sacrifices and announce at the Taizong Emperor's mountain tomb; Wencheng lay prone in grief and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi emperor acceded, he specially sent Wencheng to announce the news at Hong Taiji's tomb; Wencheng threw himself to the ground in grief and could not get up.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年八月庚戌，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: On day gengxu in the eighth month of the fifth year of Kangxi, he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the gengxu day of the eighth month of Kangxi 5, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 上親為文，遣禮部侍郎黃機諭祭，賜葬懷柔紅螺山，立碑紀績，諡文肅，御書祠額曰「元輔高風」。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally composed the funerary text, sent Ministry of Rites Vice Minister Huang Ji to announce the sacrifice, granted burial at Hongluo Mountain in Huairou, erected a stele recording his achievements, posthumous title Wensu, and imperial calligraphy for the shrine plaque reading "Yuanfu's Lofty Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the elegy himself and sent Vice Minister of Rites Huang Ji to conduct the sacrifice; he was buried at Hongluo Mountain in Huairou, with a stele recording his deeds, posthumous title Wensu, and an imperial inscription for the shrine reading "Founding Minister, Lofty Integrity."

sentences.zh: 文程子承廕、承謨、承勳、承斌、承烈、承祚，承謨自有傳。

translations.literal: Wencheng's sons were Chengyin, Chengmou, Chengxun, Chengbin, Cheng Lie, and Chengzuo; Chengmou has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng's sons were Chengyin, Chengmou, Chengxun, Chengbin, Cheng Lie, and Chengzuo; Chengmou has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 承勳字蘇公，文程第三子也。

translations.literal: Chengxun, style Sugong, was Wencheng's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun, style Sugong, was Wencheng's third son.

sentences.zh: 以任子歷官御史、郎中。

translations.literal: By privilege as hereditary appointee he served in succession as censor and director.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose to censor and bureau director.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，譚弘叛，聖祖命承勳與郎中額爾赫圖如彝陵，趣將軍噶爾漢戰，並督湖廣轉粟運軍。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi Tan Hong rebelled; the Sage Ancestor ordered Chengxun and Director E'erhetu to go to Yiling and urge General Garhan to fight, while also supervising grain transport and army supply in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 Tan Hong rebelled; the emperor sent Chengxun and Director E'erhetu to Yiling to urge General Garhan into battle and supervise grain transport for the army in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，師進攻雲南，命趣軍督餉如故。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the army advanced against Yunnan; he was ordered to urge the troops and supervise supplies as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, as the army pushed into Yunnan, he was ordered to expedite the forces and oversee supplies as before.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，還京，監崇文門稅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he returned to the capital and supervised the Chongwen Gate transit tax.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he returned to the capital and supervised the Chongwen Gate customs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上命九卿舉廉吏，承勳與焉，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the sovereign ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend honest officials; Chengxun was among them and was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend incorrupt officials; Chengxun was chosen and appointed Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授廣西巡撫，疏免容縣、鬱林州追徵陷賊後逋賦；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Guangxi governor, memorializing remission of arrears pursued in Rong county and Yulin prefecture after bandit occupation;
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he was made governor of Guangxi and memorialized to waive tax arrears still being collected in Rong county and Yulin after rebel occupation;

sentences.zh: 定諸屬徵米，本折兼納。

translations.literal: he fixed grain collection in the subordinate districts to payment in kind with commutation at assessed rates combined.
translations.idiomatic: and fixed grain levies in the subordinate districts to combined payment in kind and commuted silver.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢雲貴總督，疏定雲南援剿兩協駐軍地，裁貴州衛十五、所十，改并州縣，並增設縣七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general, memorializing to fix the encampments of the two brigades aiding suppression in Yunnan, abolishing fifteen guards and ten posts in Guizhou, merging them into prefectures and counties, and adding seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was promoted governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, fixed encampments for the two relief brigades in Yunnan, abolished fifteen guards and ten posts in Guizhou and merged them into prefectures and counties, and created seven new counties.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，湖廣兵亂，雲南時歲鑄錢，錢壅積，軍餉十之三皆予錢，軍勿便。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year troops mutinied in Huguang; Yunnan was then casting coin yearly, coin piled up in glut, and a third of army pay was given in cash, which the troops found inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 there was mutiny in Huguang; Yunnan was minting coin annually, cash piled up unused, and a third of army pay was issued in coin, which the troops disliked.

sentences.zh: 會移左協赴尋甸，遂鼓譟為變，省城兵亦將起應，承勳誅其渠二十一人，亂乃弭。

translations.literal: When the Left Brigade was moved to Xundian they then clamored and mutinied; capital garrison troops were also about to rise in response; Chengxun executed twenty-one ringleaders and the disturbance was quelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Left Brigade was ordered to Xundian the men mutinied; garrison troops in the provincial capital were about to join; Chengxun executed twenty-one ringleaders and the trouble subsided.

sentences.zh: 遂疏罷雲南鑄錢，以銀供餉。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to abolish Yunnan coin casting and supply pay in silver.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to stop Yunnan's mint and pay troops in silver.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，番阿所殺土目魯姐走匿東川土婦安氏所，𢗝出掠為民害。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Fan A'suo killed native officer Lu Jie, who fled and hid with the An clan woman of Dongchuan; he led raids out, harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 Fan A'suo killed native officer Lu Jie, who fled to the Dongchuan woman of the An clan; Fan A'suo led raids that preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上命郎中溫葆會承勳等如東川檄安氏獻阿所，斬之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the sovereign ordered Director Wen Bao to join Chengxun and others to go to Dongchuan and order the An clan to surrender A'suo, then behead him.
translations.idiomatic: On report the emperor sent Director Wen Bao with Chengxun and others to Dongchuan to demand that the An clan hand over A'suo, who was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 雲南自吳三桂亂後，康熙二十一年訖二十七年，逋屯賦當補徵，承勳疏請分年附徵，上命悉蠲之。

translations.literal: From Wu Sangui's rebellion in Yunnan, from the twenty-first year of Kangxi through the twenty-seventh year, arrears on garrison land tax were due for supplementary collection; Chengxun memorialized to collect them attached year by year; the sovereign ordered them all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison land-tax arrears in Yunnan dating from Wu Sangui's rebellion, from Kangxi 21 through year 27, were due for collection; Chengxun asked to recover them in installments; the emperor ordered a full remission.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，疏定雲南秋糧，本折兼納，貴州提督馬三奇請軍餉折銀，承勳疏言：「折賤困兵，折貴病民，宜以時損益。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he memorialized fixing Yunnan autumn grain levy with kind and commutation combined; Guizhou provincial military commissioner Ma Sanqi asked to commute army pay to silver; Chengxun memorialized: "Low commutation oppresses the troops, high commutation harms the people; the rate should be adjusted in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he fixed Yunnan's autumn grain to combined kind and commuted payment; when Guizhou commissioner Ma Sanqi proposed silver commutation for army pay, Chengxun wrote: "Low rates hurt the troops, high rates hurt the people; the rate should be adjusted as conditions change.

sentences.zh: 秋成，各府察巿值，本折兼納。」

translations.literal: At autumn harvest each prefecture should examine market prices and collect with kind and commutation combined."
translations.idiomatic: At harvest each prefecture should check market prices and collect in kind and silver together."

sentences.zh: 三十一年，疏設永北鎮，罷洱海營，增置大理府城守將吏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he memorialized establishing Yongbei garrison, abolishing Erhai camp, and adding defenders and officials for Dali prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he established Yongbei garrison, abolished Erhai camp, and added posts to guard Dali city.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he came to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he came to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 he was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六月，江南江西總督傅拉塔卒，上難其人，以授承勳。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Jiangnan-Jiangxi governor-general Fulata died; the sovereign found no suitable man and invested Chengxun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Fulata, governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi, died; finding no suitable successor, the emperor appointed Chengxun.

sentences.zh: 並諭：「承勳堅定平易，當勝此任。」

translations.literal: And instructed: "Chengxun is steady and even-tempered; he should excel in this post."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Chengxun is steady and straightforward; he should serve well."

sentences.zh: 承勳上官，琉移鳳陽關監督駐正陽關。

translations.literal: Chengxun took office and memorialized to move the Fengyang Pass supervisor to Zhengyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun took office and memorialized to move the Fengyang Pass superintendent to Zhengyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 江西民納糧，出貲俾吏輸省城，謂之腳價，尋以違例追入官，承勳疏請罷追，部議不可，上特允其請。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi people delivered grain tax they paid cash for clerks to deliver to the provincial capital, called "foot price"; soon this was pursued as illegal and confiscated to government; Chengxun memorialized to stop the pursuit; the ministry deliberated against it; the sovereign specially granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi taxpayers had paid "porters' fees" for clerks to carry grain to the provincial capital; when these were ordered confiscated as illegal, Chengxun asked to halt collection; the ministry refused, but the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 江南地卑濕，倉穀易朽蠹，承勳疏請「江蘇、安徽諸州縣，歲春夏間，以倉穀十二三平糶，出陳易新」。

translations.literal: Jiangnan land is low and damp, granary grain easily rots and is worm-eaten; Chengxun memorialized: "In Jiangsu and Anhui prefectures and counties, each spring and summer release one or two tenths of granary grain at fair sale to replace old with new."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan's low, damp terrain spoiled stored grain easily; Chengxun asked that "each spring and summer Jiangsu and Anhui sell one tenth to two tenths of granary stores at fair price to rotate stock."

sentences.zh: 又以江南賦重，疏請「州縣經徵分數，視續完多寡為輕重。

translations.literal: Again because Jiangnan taxes were heavy, he memorialized: "Prefectural and county collection quotas should be weighted light or heavy according to how much arrears have been cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiangnan's tax burden was heavy, he also asked that "collection quotas vary with how much each district had cleared its arrears.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年後逋賦分年附徵，俾寬吏議，紓民力」。

translations.literal: Arrears after the eighteenth year of Kangxi should be collected attached over years, to ease official evaluation and relieve the people."
translations.idiomatic: Arrears after Kangxi 18 should be recovered in installments, easing pressure on officials and taxpayers."

sentences.zh: 皆如議行。

translations.literal: All were enacted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.
