sentences.zh: 三十五年，淮、揚、徐諸府災，疏請發省倉米十萬石，續借京口留漕鳳倉存麥，治賑，民賴以全。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Huai, Yang, and Xu prefectures suffered disaster; he memorialized to issue one hundred thousand piculs of rice from provincial granaries, then borrow stored wheat retained from grain transport at Jingkou and Feng granaries for relief, and the people were preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 flood struck the Huai, Yang, and Xu districts; he released one hundred thousand piculs from provincial granaries and drew on wheat held at Jingkou and Feng for relief, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，命監修高家堰堤工。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was ordered to supervise repair of the Gaojiayan dike works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 he was ordered to oversee repairs on the Gaojiayan dikes.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，工成，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year the work was completed and he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 the work was finished and he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 53.

sentences.zh: 承勳初授廣西巡撫，入辭，上誡之曰：「汝父兄皆為國宣力，汝當潔己愛民，毋信幕僚，沽名妄作。」

translations.literal: When Chengxun was first appointed Guangxi governor and came to take leave, the sovereign admonished him: "Your father and elder brothers all expended strength for the state; you must keep yourself pure and love the people, do not trust staff secretaries, and seek reputation by reckless acts."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengxun was first appointed governor of Guangxi and came to take leave, the emperor warned him: "Your father and brothers served the state; keep yourself honest, care for the people, do not trust secretarial staff, and do not court reputation by reckless acts."

sentences.zh: 及自云貴總督入覲，上方謁孝陵，承勳迎謁米峪口，上曰：「汝父兄先朝舊臣，汝兄复盡節。

translations.literal: When he came from Yunnan-Guizhou governor-generalship for audience, the sovereign was paying respects at the Xiaoling tomb; Chengxun met him at Miyukou; the sovereign said: "Your father and elder brothers were old ministers of the previous dynasty; your elder brother Fu died in loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from Yunnan-Guizhou for audience, the emperor was visiting the Xiaoling tomb; Chengxun met him at Miyukou. The emperor said: "Your father and brothers were ministers of the founding court; your brother Fu died in loyal service.

sentences.zh: 朕見汝因思汝兄，心為軫戚。

translations.literal: Seeing you I think of your brother, and my heart is wrung with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing you reminds me of your brother, and my heart aches.

sentences.zh: 不見汝八九年，汝鬚髮遂皓白如此。

translations.literal: I have not seen you for eight or nine years, yet your beard and hair have turned so white.
translations.idiomatic: I have not seen you for eight or nine years, yet your hair has turned so white.

sentences.zh: 郊外苦寒，以朕所禦貂冠、貂褂、狐白裘賜汝。

translations.literal: It is bitter cold in the suburbs; I bestow on you the sable cap, sable jacket, and white-fox fur I wear myself.
translations.idiomatic: It is bitter cold in the suburbs; take the sable cap, sable jacket, and white-fox fur I wear myself.

sentences.zh: 汝且勿更衣，慮中風寒。

translations.literal: Do not change clothes yet, lest you catch cold.
translations.idiomatic: Do not change clothes yet, lest you catch cold.

sentences.zh: 明日可服以謝。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow you may wear them to give thanks."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow you may wear them to give thanks."

sentences.zh: 聖祖推文程、承謨舊恩，因厚遇承勳如是。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor, extending old favor to Wencheng and Chengmou, therefore treated Chengxun with such generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering old debts to Wencheng and Chengmou, the Kangxi emperor treated Chengxun with such warmth.

sentences.zh: 時繹，承勳子。

translations.literal: Shiyi was Chengxun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi was Chengxun's son.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，自佐領三遷為馬蘭鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongzheng reign, from zuoling he was transferred three ranks to become commander of Malan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng he rose in three steps from zuoling to Malan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，命署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made acting governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 是年，遷正藍旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to be dutong of the Chinese Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became dutong of the Chinese Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 五年，移鑲白旗漢軍都統，並署總督如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he moved to Chinese Bordered White Banner dutong and continued as acting governor-general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to Chinese Bordered White Banner dutong while remaining acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十二月，時繹疏：「請自雍正六年始，江蘇、安徽各州縣應徵丁銀，均入地畝內徵收。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Shiyi memorialized: "From the sixth year of Yongzheng onward, let poll-tax silver due from each Jiangsu and Anhui prefecture and county be collected together within land-tax fields."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shiyi memorialized: "From Yongzheng year 6 onward, poll tax in Jiangsu and Anhui should be merged into the land tax."

sentences.zh: 地丁並徵始此。

translations.literal: Combined land-and-poll collection began here.
translations.idiomatic: Combined land-and-poll collection began with this measure.

sentences.zh: 六年，授戶部尚書，仍署總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue while still acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made Minister of Revenue while remaining acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時繹在官，嘗疏請就通州運河入海處，作涵洞以時蓄洩。

translations.literal: While in office Shiyi once memorialized to build culverts at the Tongzhou canal's outlet to the sea for timely storage and release.
translations.idiomatic: In office he once proposed culverts at the Tongzhou canal mouth to regulate storage and release.

sentences.zh: 規揚州水利，濬海口，疏車路、白塗、海溝諸水，泰州運鹽河為之堤。

translations.literal: He planned Yangzhou waterworks, dredged the sea mouth, cleared the Chelu, Baitu, and Haigou waterways, and built dikes along Taizhou's salt transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: He planned Yangzhou waterworks, dredged the estuary, cleared the Chelu, Baitu, and Haigou channels, and diked Taizhou's salt canal.

sentences.zh: 鹽城、如皋諸水入海處，為之閘若涵洞。

translations.literal: At the sea outlets of Yancheng, Rugao, and other waterways he built sluices like culverts.
translations.idiomatic: At Yancheng, Rugao, and other outlets to the sea he built sluices and culverts.

sentences.zh: 釐兩淮鹽政，增漕標廟灣、鹽城二營兵吏。

translations.literal: He reformed the Lianghuai salt administration and added troops and clerks to the grain-transport and salt garrisons at Miaowan and Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the Lianghuai salt administration and added troops and clerks to the Miaowan and Yancheng transport garrisons.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the ministries and approved.

sentences.zh: 上以蘇、松諸處多盜，時繹戢盜才絀，命以江蘇七府五州盜案屬浙江總督李衛。

translations.literal: Because Su and Song districts had many bandits and Shiyi was inadequate at suppressing bandits, the sovereign ordered Jiangsu's seven prefectures and five subprefectures' bandit cases assigned to Zhejiang governor-general Li Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Because banditry was rife in Suzhou and Songjiang and Shiyi proved weak at suppression, the emperor assigned cases in Jiangsu's seven prefectures and five subprefectures to Zhejiang governor-general Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 衛名捕江寧民張云如以符呪惑眾謀不軌，而時繹嘗與往還，衛因論劾。

translations.literal: Li Wei famously arrested Jiangning commoner Zhang Yunru for using talismans and incantations to delude the crowd and plot sedition; Shiyi had once associated with him, and Li Wei therefore impeached Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei arrested the Jiangning man Zhang Yunru on charges of sedition through charms and sorcery; because Shiyi had associated with Zhang, Li Wei impeached him.

sentences.zh: 八年，命尚書李永昇會鞫得實，誅云如，解時繹任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the sovereign ordered Minister Li Yongsheng to join in trial and establish the facts; Zhang Yunru was executed and Shiyi was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the emperor ordered Minister Li Yongsheng to investigate; Zhang was executed and Shiyi was removed.

sentences.zh: 召還京，命董理太平峪吉地。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital and ordered to oversee the auspicious site at Taiping Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and put in charge of the Taiping Valley imperial tomb site.

sentences.zh: 旋復命協理河東河務，河東總督田文鏡復以誤工論劾，諭曰：「朕以范時繹為勳臣後，加以擢用。

translations.literal: Soon he was again ordered to assist in Hedong river conservancy; Hedong governor-general Tian Wenjing again impeached him for faulty works, and an edict said: "I promoted Fan Shiyi because he is the descendant of a meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again assigned to Hedong river works; when Hedong governor-general Tian Wenjing impeached him for faulty construction, the emperor wrote: "I promoted Fan Shiyi as the descendant of a meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 硃鴻緒嘗奏時繹廉，至日用不能給，朕深為動念，優與養廉。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongxu once memorialized that Shiyi was honest yet could not meet daily expenses; I was deeply moved and generously granted him integrity-support stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongxu once said Shiyi was honest but could not make ends meet; I was moved and gave him extra integrity stipends.

sentences.zh: 後知時繹例所當得，未嘗不取。

translations.literal: Later I learned that what Shiyi was entitled to by regulation, he never failed to take.
translations.idiomatic: Later I learned he never failed to take what regulations allowed.

sentences.zh: 朕猶令增糈，蓋欲遂成其廉，使殫心力於封疆也。

translations.literal: I still ordered increased grain rations, intending thereby to complete his integrity and make him devote his whole mind to frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: I still increased his grain allowance, hoping to make him truly honest and devote himself to his post.

sentences.zh: 顧時繹袒私交，容姦宄，朕复密諭李衛善為保全。

translations.literal: Yet Shiyi showed favor to private associates and harbored criminals; I again secretly instructed Li Wei to preserve him as far as possible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he favored private associates and sheltered criminals; I secretly told Li Wei to protect him when he could.

sentences.zh: 且范氏為大僚者，惟時繹及其從弟時捷，勳臣後裔，漸至零落，朕心不忍，所以委曲成全之者至矣。

translations.literal: Among the Fan clan who were great officials, only Shiyi and his cousin Shijie remained; as descendants of meritorious ministers they had gradually fallen to ruin, and my heart could not bear it—so the care with which I bent to preserve them was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Fan great officials only Shiyi and his cousin Shijie remained; as meritorious descendants they had fallen on hard times, and I spared no effort to preserve them.

sentences.zh: 復命協理河務，豈意伏汛危急，時繹安坐於旁，置國事弁髦，視民命草芥。

translations.literal: When he was again ordered to assist in river works, who would have thought that at the height of the flood season Shiyi would sit at ease to one side, treating state affairs as a discarded cap tassel and the people's lives as grass?
translations.idiomatic: When he was again assigned to river works, at the height of flood season he sat idle, treating state affairs lightly and people's lives cheaply.

sentences.zh: 負恩瘝職，他人尚不可，況時繹乎？」

translations.literal: To betray grace and be negligent in office—this is intolerable in others, how much more in Shiyi?"
translations.idiomatic: Betraying imperial favor and neglecting duty is intolerable in anyone—how much more in Shiyi?"

sentences.zh: 逮治，部議坐云如獄論斬，上复特宥之。

translations.literal: He was arrested and tried; the ministry deliberated sentencing by the Zhang Yunru case to decapitation; the sovereign again specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested; the ministry recommended execution under the Zhang Yunru precedent, but the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 授鑲藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice dutong of the Chinese Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice dutong of the Chinese Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 十年，授工部尚書，兼鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made Minister of Works and Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner dutong.

sentences.zh: 十二年，罷尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was dismissed from the ministry post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was dismissed as minister.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復以侍衛保柱劾行賄，下部議罪，尋遇赦。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the bodyguard Baozhu again impeached him for bribery; the case was referred to the ministry for sentencing, but he soon met an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 the guardsman Baozhu impeached him for bribery; sentencing was referred to the ministry, but he was soon amnestied.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 6.

sentences.zh: 承斌，文程第四子，襲一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Chengbin, Wencheng's fourth son, inherited first-class jingkini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbin, Wencheng's fourth son, inherited first-class jingkini hafan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 時捷，承斌子。

translations.literal: Shijie was Chengbin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie was Chengbin's son.

sentences.zh: 自參領再遷為陝西、寧夏總兵。

translations.literal: From canling he was again promoted to regional commander of Shaanxi and Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from canling to regional commander of Shaanxi and Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年，署陝甘提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi he served as acting Shaanxi-Gansu provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 57 he acted as Shaanxi-Gansu provincial military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed Shaanxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was made governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷鑲白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Chinese Bordered White Banner dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became Chinese Bordered White Banner dutong.

sentences.zh: 五年，年羹堯得罪，世宗以羹堯嘗舉時捷，及羹堯敗，事連時捷，罷都統，授侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Nian Gengyao fell from grace; the Shizong Emperor, because Gengyao had once recommended Shijie, and when Gengyao fell the matter implicated Shijie, dismissed him as dutong and appointed him guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Nian Gengyao fell; because Gengyao had once recommended Shijie, Yongzheng implicated Shijie, removed him as dutong, and made him a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 八年，授散秩大臣，護陵寢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed minister without portfolio and charged to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made minister without portfolio and assigned to guard the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 是時，時捷從兄時繹以協理河東河務誤工罷黜，世宗以文程諸孫無為大僚者，命時捷署古北口提督，直隸總兵官聽節制，詔勉以改過。

translations.literal: At that time his cousin Shiyi had been dismissed for faulty Hedong river works; the Shizong Emperor, seeing that none of Wencheng's grandsons held great office, ordered Shijie to act as Gubeikou provincial military commissioner, with Zhili regional commanders under his direction, and issued an edict to him to reform his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Shiyi was dismissed for faulty Hedong river works, Yongzheng, finding no Fan descendant in high office, made Shijie acting Gubeikou commissioner with Zhili commanders under him and urged him to reform.

sentences.zh: 旋移陝西固原提督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guyuan provincial military commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Guyuan commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，例改一等子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, by regulation he was changed to first-class viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 his rank was changed by regulation to first-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 二年，以病召還，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year, because of illness he was recalled and appointed minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 illness brought his recall and appointment as minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 3.

sentences.zh: 建中，時捷孫，襲一等男。

translations.literal: Jianzhong, Shijie's grandson, inherited first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong, Shijie's grandson, inherited first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 自副參領再遷副都統、侍郎。

translations.literal: From deputy canling he was again promoted to vice dutong and vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from deputy canling to vice dutong and vice minister.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，授戶部尚書，署正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was appointed Minister of Revenue and acting Chinese Plain Yellow Banner dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he was made Minister of Revenue and acting Chinese Plain Yellow Banner dutong.

sentences.zh: 尋改都察院左都御史，出為杭州將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and sent out as Hangzhou garrison general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Left Censor-in-Chief and was posted as Hangzhou garrison general.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，諡恪慎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; posthumous title Ke-shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 5, with posthumous title Ke-shen.

sentences.zh: 時綬，文程諸孫。

translations.literal: Shishou was among Wencheng's grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Shishou was a grandson of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，自筆帖式累遷至戶部郎中。

translations.literal: During Yongzheng, from clerk of the Grand Council he rose in succession to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he rose from Grand Council clerk to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，复累遷至湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he again rose in succession to Hubei provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he rose again to Hubei administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署湖南巡撫，疏言：「湘陰、益陽諸縣，察有私墾千餘頃，皆瀕洞庭，歲旱方穫，請緩昇科。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, as acting Hunan governor, he memorialized: "In Xiangyin, Yiyang, and other counties more than a thousand qing of private reclamation on the Dongting margin have been found; all border Dongting Lake, and the year is dry just as harvest comes—please defer promotion to taxable status.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, as acting governor of Hunan, he reported: "Xiangyin, Yiyang, and other counties had over a thousand qing of private reclamation along Dongting, all just harvested after drought, and asked to defer taxing the new fields.

sentences.zh: 洞庭諸私垸窒水道，勸禁增築。」

translations.literal: The various private embankments at Dongting obstruct the waterways; he urged prohibition of further construction."
translations.idiomatic: Private embankments around Dongting were choking the waterways; he urged a ban on further construction."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 十八年，移江西巡撫，病免。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred as Jiangxi governor and relieved due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he became governor of Jiangxi but was soon relieved due to illness.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起授戶部侍郎，署都統，請赴西路屯田。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and acting dutong, requesting assignment to military colonies on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and acting dutong and asked to serve on the western colonial frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，副都統定長劾時綬役兵漁利，遣使就讞，時綬未嘗役兵，特其僕從藉事求利，命奪官，交定長責自效。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Vice Dutong Ding Chang impeached Shishou for using soldiers to fish for profit; an envoy was sent to try the case. Shishou had never used soldiers—only his servants had used affairs to seek profit. He was ordered stripped of office and handed over to Ding Chang to redeem himself by merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Vice Dutong Ding Chang accused Shishou of profiteering through soldiers; an investigator was sent. Shishou had not used soldiers himself—only his servants had exploited their position. He was stripped of rank and placed under Ding Chang's supervision to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授頭等侍衛，遷鑲藍旗漢軍副都統、吏部侍郎、哈爾沙爾辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed First-class Bodyguard and promoted to Chinese Bordered Blue Banner vice dutong, Vice Minister of Personnel, and commissioner for Halsar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he became a First-class Bodyguard and rose to Chinese Bordered Blue Banner vice dutong, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Halsar commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，遷左都御史，仍留哈爾沙爾辦事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief while retaining his Halsar commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he became Left Censor-in-Chief but kept his Halsar post.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he was made governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 入對，上以時綬弱不能任封疆，三十三年，复授都統、左都御史。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at audience, the sovereign held that Shishou was too weak to bear frontier responsibility; in the thirty-third year he was again appointed dutong and Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor judged Shishou too frail for a frontier post; in year 33 he was restored as dutong and Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷。

translations.literal: The next year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 47.

sentences.zh: 時紀，亦文程諸孫。

translations.literal: Shiji was also among Wencheng's grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was another of Wencheng's grandsons.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以任子授工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, by privilege as hereditary appointee he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he entered the Ministry of Works as a hereditary appointee.

sentences.zh: 四遷，署廣東按察使。

translations.literal: After four promotions he was acting Guangdong provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he served as acting Guangdong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，俸滿入覲，諭范氏無大僚，授鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when his salary term was complete and he presented himself at court, he was told the Fan clan lacked high officials and was appointed Chinese Bordered Red Banner vice dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25, at the end of his salary term and court audience, he was told the Fan clan had no senior ministers and was made Chinese Bordered Red Banner vice dutong.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he became Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，疏請就京南諸州縣開田植稻，下直隸總督方觀承察土宜酌行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he memorialized requesting that fields south of the capital be opened to plant rice; the matter was referred to Zhili Governor Fang Guancheng to examine soil suitability and act as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he asked to open farmland south of the capital for rice; Zhili Governor Fang Guancheng was ordered to inspect local conditions and proceed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 屢移倉場、戶部、禮部諸侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred among the vice ministries of the Granary, Revenue, and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He moved repeatedly among vice-ministerial posts at the Granary, Revenue, and Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，以年衰改副都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, because of advanced age, he was changed to vice dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42, on account of age, he was reassigned as vice dutong.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 宜恆，時綬子。

translations.literal: Yiheng was Shishou's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yiheng was Shishou's son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，自鑾儀衛、整儀衛，五遷，為福建福寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: During Qianlong, from the Imperial Procession Guard and the Ceremonial Guard he rose through five promotions to become regional commander of Funing Garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he rose through five posts from the procession guards to regional commander of Fujian's Funing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，授正藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was appointed Chinese Plain Blue Banner vice dutong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 47 he became Chinese Plain Blue Banner vice dutong.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 he became Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 2.

sentences.zh: 文程曾孫行又有宜清，乾隆間官盛京工部侍郎；

translations.literal: Among Wencheng's great-grandsons in the Xing branch there was also Yiqing, who in the Qianlong period served as Vice Minister of Works at Mukden;
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng's great-grandson Yiqing, of the Xing branch, served as Mukden Vice Minister of Works under Qianlong;

sentences.zh: 四世諸孫建豐，嘉慶時官吏部侍郎：皆以漢軍任滿缺，一時稱異數云。

translations.literal: and Jianfeng, a fourth-generation descendant, was Vice Minister of Personnel in the Jiaqing period: all held Manchu vacancies as Chinese Bannermen, and for a time this was called a remarkable exception.
translations.idiomatic: and fourth-generation descendant Jianfeng was Vice Minister of Personnel under Jiaqing—all of them holding Manchu posts as Chinese Bannermen, which for a time was hailed as an extraordinary exception.

sentences.zh: 寧完我，字公甫，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Ning Wanwo, style Gongfu, was a man of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Wanwo, style Gongfu, was from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 天命間來歸，給事貝勒薩哈廉家，隸漢軍正紅旗。

translations.literal: In the Tianming era he came over and submitted; he was assigned to Prince Sahalian's household and was registered under the Chinese Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted in the Tianming era, served in Prince Sahalian's household, and was enrolled in the Chinese Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，太宗聞完我通文史，召令直文館。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong the Taizong Emperor heard that Wanwo was versed in letters and history and summoned him to serve in the Literary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 Hong Taiji learned that Wanwo was learned in letters and history and summoned him to the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 完我入對，薦所知者與之同升，鮑承先其一也。

translations.literal: When Wanwo entered audience he recommended men he knew for joint promotion; Bao Chengxian was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Wanwo recommended several acquaintances for promotion with him; Bao Chengxian was among them.

sentences.zh: 尋授參將。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a brigadier general.

sentences.zh: 四年，師克永平，命與達海宣諭安撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the army took Yongping, he was ordered with Dahai to proclaim and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, after Yongping fell, he and Dahai were ordered to proclaim the victory and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 又從攻大凌河及招撫察哈爾，皆有功，授世職備禦。

translations.literal: He also followed in the attack on Dalinghe and in winning over the Chahar, all with merit, and was granted the hereditary rank of company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the siege of Dalinghe and the pacification of the Chahar, earning merit each time, and was granted a hereditary company commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，初置六部，命儒臣賜號「榜式」得仍舊稱，餘稱「筆帖式」。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, seventh month, when the Six Ministries were first established, Confucian officials were granted the title "Bangshi" and might keep their former designation; the rest were called "bitchi shi."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 5, when the Six Ministries were first set up, scholar-officials honored as "Bangshi" could keep their old titles; the rest were called "bitchi shi."

sentences.zh: 完我遇事敢言，嘗議定官制，辨服色。

translations.literal: Wanwo spoke boldly whenever affairs arose; he once discussed fixing the official system and distinguishing dress by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo spoke his mind on every issue; he once helped define the bureaucracy and distinguish official dress.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上疏言：「自古設官定職，非帝王好為鋪張。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he memorialized: "Since antiquity the establishment of offices and fixing of duties has not been because kings love extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he memorialized: "Since antiquity, kings have not created offices out of love of display.

sentences.zh: 慮國事無綱紀也，置六部；

translations.literal: Fearing that state affairs would lack discipline, they set up the Six Ministries;
translations.idiomatic: They feared affairs of state would lack order, and so set up the Six Ministries;

sentences.zh: 慮六部有偏私也，置六科；

translations.literal: fearing partiality in the Six Ministries, they set up the Six Offices of Scrutiny;
translations.idiomatic: they feared the ministries would grow partial, and so set up the Six Offices of Scrutiny;

sentences.zh: 慮君心宜啟沃也，置館臣；

translations.literal: fearing the sovereign's mind should lack counsel, they set up academicians;
translations.idiomatic: they feared the ruler's mind would lack wise counsel, and so set up academicians;

sentences.zh: 慮下情或壅蔽也，置通政。

translations.literal: fearing that sentiments below might be blocked, they set up the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: they feared the people's voice might be stifled, and so set up the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 數事相因，缺一不可。

translations.literal: These matters depend on one another; not one may be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Each depends on the others; not one can be spared.

sentences.zh: 上不立言官，不過謂我國人人得以進言，何必言官。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not establish remonstrating officials, only saying that in our state everyone may advance words—why need remonstrating officials?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not established remonstrating officials, saying only that in our state everyone may speak up—so why need censors?

sentences.zh: 臣請明辨之，我國六部既立，曾見有一人抗顏論劾者否？

translations.literal: Your servant asks to distinguish this clearly: now that our Six Ministries are established, has one ever been seen who with set face impeached and debated?
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to see the difference: the Six Ministries are in place—has anyone ever stood up to impeach or debate?

sentences.zh: 似此寂寂，豈國中真無事耶？

translations.literal: In such silence, can it be that in the state there is truly nothing to report?
translations.idiomatic: In such silence, can the realm truly have no wrongs to report?

sentences.zh: 舉國然諾浮沉，以狡滑為圓活，以容隱為公道，以優柔退縮為雅重，上皇皇圖治，亦何樂有此景像也？

translations.literal: The whole state nods assent and sinks or floats; craftiness is taken for tact, concealment for fairness, timid retreat for refinement—what pleasure can Your Majesty take in such a scene while earnestly seeking good government?
translations.idiomatic: The whole court nods along: craftiness passes for tact, concealment for fairness, timid retreat for refinement—what joy can Your Majesty take in such a scene while striving to govern well?

sentences.zh: 況今日秉政者，豈盡循理方正？

translations.literal: Moreover, those who hold power today—are they all upright and principled?
translations.idiomatic: And are those in power today all upright and principled?

sentences.zh: 屬僚既不敢非長官，局外又誰敢議權貴？

translations.literal: Subordinates dare not criticize their superiors, and who outside the circle dares discuss the powerful?
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates dare not criticize their chiefs, and who outside the inner circle dares question the powerful?

sentences.zh: 臣知國中事，上亦時得聞知，然不過猶古之告密，孰若置言官，興利除害，皆公言之之為愈耶？

translations.literal: Your servant knows affairs in the state, and Your Majesty also sometimes hears of them; yet this is no more than the secret denunciations of old—how is it not better to set up remonstrating officials, remove harm and advance benefit, and let all be spoken openly?
translations.idiomatic: I know what happens in the state, and Your Majesty sometimes hears of it too—but that is only the old game of secret denunciation. How is it not better to appoint censors, purge abuses and advance the good, and let everything be said in the open?

sentences.zh: 言官既設，君身尚許指摘，他人更何忌諱？

translations.literal: Once remonstrating officials are established, even the sovereign's person may be criticized—what further need for reserve among others?
translations.idiomatic: Once censors exist, even the sovereign may be criticized—what further restraint need others feel?

sentences.zh: 苟不至貪污欺誑，任其盡言，勿為禁制，此古帝王明目達聰之妙術也。

translations.literal: If they are not corrupt or deceitful, let them speak fully and do not forbid them—this is the subtle art by which ancient kings kept bright eyes and keen ears.
translations.idiomatic: So long as they are not corrupt or deceitful, let them speak freely without restraint—this is how ancient kings kept their eyes bright and their ears keen.

sentences.zh: 若謂南朝言官敗壞，此自其君鑑別不明，非其初定制之不善也。

translations.literal: If one says the remonstrating officials of the Southern Court were ruined, that was because their sovereign's discernment was unclear—not because the original institution was unsound.
translations.idiomatic: If one blames the censors of the Ming for ruin, the fault lay in the ruler's poor judgment—not in the institution itself.

sentences.zh: 我國'筆帖式'，漢言'書房'，朝廷安所用書房？

translations.literal: In our state 'bitchi shi,' in Chinese 'study rooms'—of what use are study rooms in court?
translations.idiomatic: In our state the 'bitchi shi'—in Chinese, 'study rooms'—what use has the court for study rooms?

sentences.zh: 官生雜處，名器弗定。

translations.literal: Officials and clerks are mixed together; titles and ranks are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and clerks are thrown together; titles and ranks are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 不置通政，則下情上壅，勵精圖治之謂何也？

translations.literal: If the Office of Transmission is not set up, sentiment below is blocked above—what then of striving to govern well?
translations.idiomatic: Without the Office of Transmission, the voice below is choked off above—what becomes of earnest government?

sentences.zh: 至若服制，尤陶鎔滿、漢第一急事。

translations.literal: As for dress regulations, these are above all the first urgent matter in forging unity between Manchu and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: As for dress regulations, nothing is more urgent for forging unity between Manchu and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 上遇漢官，溫慰懇至，而國人反陵轢之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty treats Chinese officials with warm and earnest consolation, yet our countrymen in turn bully them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty greets Chinese officials with warm and earnest kindness, yet our own people bully them in turn.

sentences.zh: 漢官不通滿語，每以此被辱，有至傷心墮淚者，將何以招徠遠人，使成一體？

translations.literal: Chinese officials do not know Manchu and are often insulted for it; some have been hurt to tears—how then win over distant men and make one body?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese officials do not know Manchu and are often humiliated for it; some have wept in grief—how then are distant men to be won and made one with us?

sentences.zh: 故臣謂分別服色，所繫至大，原上勿再忽之也。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant holds that distinguishing dress by color bears on matters of the greatest weight; I pray Your Majesty not to neglect it again.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I say distinguishing dress by rank matters profoundly; I pray Your Majesty not to neglect it again.

sentences.zh: 臣等非才，惟耿介忠悃，至死不變。

translations.literal: We your servants lack talent; only our upright loyalty, unchanged to death.
translations.idiomatic: We lack talent; only our stubborn loyalty, unchanged to the death.

sentences.zh: 昨年副將高鴻中出領甲喇額真，臣具疏請留；

translations.literal: Last year Brigadier General Gao Hongzhong went out to command an ala; your servant memorialized asking that he remain;
translations.idiomatic: Last year Brigadier General Gao Hongzhong left to command an ala; I memorialized asking that he stay;

sentences.zh: 今游擊范文程又補刑曹，諒臣亦不得久居文館。

translations.literal: now Guerrilla Colonel Fan Wencheng has again been assigned to the Board of Punishments—I fear your servant too cannot long remain in the Literary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: now Guerrilla Colonel Fan Wencheng has been posted to the Board of Punishments—I fear I too cannot long remain at the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 若臣等二三人皆去，豈復得慷慨為上盡言乎？」

translations.literal: If two or three of us your servants all depart, how can we again speak boldly and exhaust ourselves for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If two or three of us are all removed, who will speak boldly and exhaust himself for Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，上頗韙之，命俟次第舉行。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the sovereign largely approved and ordered that it be carried out in due order.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was largely approved, and the emperor ordered its measures carried out step by step.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，完我疏言：「昨年十一月初九日，自大凌河旋師，上豫議今年進取，至誠惻怛，推心置腹，藹然家人父子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Wanwo memorialized: "On the ninth day of the eleventh month last year, as the army returned from Dalinghe, Your Majesty pre-discussed this year's advance; sincerity and compassion were utmost, heart laid open and belly exposed, kindly as father and son in one household.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 6 Wanwo memorialized: "On the ninth of the eleventh month last year, as the army returned from Dalinghe, Your Majesty spoke in advance of this year's campaign with utmost sincerity and compassion, heart open and trust complete, kindly as father and son under one roof.

sentences.zh: 臣敢不殫精畢思，用效駑鈍。

translations.literal: How dare your servant not exhaust mind and thought to offer his feeble effort?
translations.idiomatic: How could I not exhaust my mind to offer what little strength I have?

sentences.zh: 臣聞千里而戰，雖勝亦敗。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: to fight a thousand li away, though victorious, is still defeat.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said: to fight a thousand li from home is defeat even in victory.

sentences.zh: 近年將士貪欺之習，大異於先帝時，更張而轉移之。

translations.literal: In recent years the habit of greed and deceit among officers and soldiers differs greatly from the Former Emperor's time; it must be changed and turned about.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years officers and soldiers have grown greedy and deceitful as never in the Former Emperor's day; the habit must be broken and turned about.

sentences.zh: 上固切切在念，而曾未顯斡旋之術。

translations.literal: Your Majesty indeed keeps this close at heart, yet has never shown a clear art of turning the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps this close at heart, yet has never shown a clear way to turn the tide.

sentences.zh: 人心不鍊，必不得指臂相使之用。

translations.literal: If hearts are not tempered, one cannot obtain the use of directing them like arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: Unless hearts are tempered, you cannot command men as you would your own arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 分軍駐防，萬難調停，雖諸葛復生，無能為也。

translations.literal: Dividing the army for garrison duty is utterly hard to harmonize; though Zhuge Liang were reborn, nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting the army for garrison duty is impossible to harmonize; even if Zhuge Liang were reborn, he could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 又況蜂蠆有毒，肘腋患生，疑貳之祖大壽，率寧、錦瘡痍之眾，坐伺於數百里間，杞人之見，不得不慮及也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, wasps and scorpions have poison; trouble at the armpits may arise; the doubtful Zu Dashou leads the wounded masses of Ning and Jin, sitting in wait within several hundred li—a fretful man's fear cannot but be taken into account."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover wasps and scorpions have their sting; trouble may breed at your elbow: the disloyal Zu Dashou leads Ning and Jin's wounded masses, watching from hundreds of li away—a man's idle dread, yet it cannot be ignored."

sentences.zh: 三月，上決策自將伐察哈爾，而完我以為大凌河降卒思遁，宜先圖山海，還取錦州，因上疏諫。

translations.literal: In the third month the sovereign decided to lead the army himself against the Chahar; Wanwo held that the surrendered troops of Dalinghe were thinking of flight, and that one should first take Shanhai and then recover Jinzhou, and so memorialized in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor decided to lead the campaign against the Chahar himself; Wanwo believed the Dalinghe surrendered troops were ripe to bolt, urged securing Shanhai Pass first and then retaking Jinzhou, and memorialized against the plan.

sentences.zh: 四月，師西出，度興安嶺，次都勒河，偵言林丹汗西走。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army marched west, crossed the Greater Khingan, halted at the Dule River; scouts reported Ligdan Khan had fled west.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army marched west, crossed the Greater Khingan, and halted at the Dule River; scouts reported Ligdan Khan had fled westward.

sentences.zh: 完我與同值文館范文程、馬國柱合疏申前議，略言：「師已度興安嶺，察哈爾望風遠遁，上威名顯襮。

translations.literal: Wanwo, together with his Literary Bureau colleagues Fan Wencheng and Ma Guozhu on duty, jointly memorialized repeating their earlier counsel, in brief: "The army has already crossed the Greater Khingan; the Chahar flee at the wind from afar; Your Majesty's martial renown shines forth.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo, with his Literary Bureau colleagues Fan Wencheng and Ma Guozhu, jointly renewed their earlier counsel: "The army has crossed the Greater Khingan; the Chahar flee before our name; Your Majesty's fame blazes abroad.

sentences.zh: 臣度上且罷西征，轉而南入。

translations.literal: Your servant judges that Your Majesty will soon halt the western expedition and turn southward.
translations.idiomatic: I judge that Your Majesty will soon halt the western campaign and turn south.

sentences.zh: 上憐士卒勞苦，不能長驅直入，徒攜子女、囊金帛而歸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities the soldiers' toil and cannot drive straight in; you will only carry off women and children and bag gold and silk home.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will pity the soldiers' hardship and be unable to drive deep; you will carry off only women, children, and bags of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 苟若是，大事去矣！

translations.literal: If it should be so, the great enterprise is lost!
translations.idiomatic: If it comes to that, the great enterprise is lost!

sentences.zh: 昔者遼左之誤，諉諸先帝；

translations.literal: In former times the error on the Liao left was blamed on the Former Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Once the failure on the Liao frontier was blamed on the Former Emperor;

sentences.zh: 永平之失，諉諸二貝勒。

translations.literal: the loss of Yongping was blamed on the Second Prince.
translations.idiomatic: the loss of Yongping on the Second Prince.

sentences.zh: 今更將誰諉？

translations.literal: On whom will blame be laid now?
translations.idiomatic: On whom will blame fall now?

sentences.zh: 信蓋天下，然後能服天下。

translations.literal: Trust must cover the realm; only then can the realm be won.
translations.idiomatic: Trust must cover the realm—only then can the realm be won.

sentences.zh: 臣等為上籌之，以為當令從軍蒙古，每人擇頭人三二輩，挾從者十餘人，從上南入，餘悉遣還部。

translations.literal: We your servants have planned for Your Majesty and hold that the Mongols following the army should each choose two or three headmen, taking a dozen or so followers, to follow Your Majesty south; the rest should all be sent back to their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: We have laid plans for Your Majesty: let each Mongol in the army choose two or three headmen with a dozen followers to march south with you, and send the rest back to their tribes.

sentences.zh: 然後嚴我法度，昭告有眾，師行所經，戒殺戒掠，務種德樹仁，宏我後來之路。

translations.literal: Then strictly enforce our laws, proclaim them to the multitude, and wherever the army passes forbid killing and plundering; strive to plant virtue and nurture benevolence and broaden the road for what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Then enforce our laws strictly, proclaim them to all, and wherever the army marches forbid killing and looting; plant virtue and nurture benevolence and widen the road ahead.

sentences.zh: 今此出師，諸軍士賣牛買馬，典衣置裝，離家益遠，見財而不取，軍心怠矣，取則又蹈覆轍。

translations.literal: On this campaign the soldiers sold oxen to buy horses, pawned clothes to equip themselves, and left home ever farther; if they see wealth and do not take it, army hearts grow slack—and if they take it, they tread the old rut again.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign soldiers sold oxen for horses and pawned their clothes to equip themselves, leaving home ever farther behind; if they see wealth and do not seize it, their hearts slacken—and if they seize it, they tread the old rut again.

sentences.zh: 上豈不曰'我厲禁取財，其孰敢違'？

translations.literal: Will not Your Majesty say, 'I sternly forbid taking wealth—who dares disobey'?
translations.idiomatic: Will not Your Majesty say, 'I have strictly forbidden looting—who would dare disobey'?

sentences.zh: 上耳目所及，或不敢犯；

translations.literal: What reaches Your Majesty's eyes and ears perhaps none dare violate;
translations.idiomatic: What reaches your eyes and ears perhaps none dare violate;

sentences.zh: 耳目所不及，孰能保者？

translations.literal: what does not reach eyes and ears—who can guarantee it?
translations.idiomatic: what lies beyond them—who can guarantee?

sentences.zh: 無問蒙古部長，及諸貝勒，稍稍擾民，怨歸於上，此上所當深思者也。

translations.literal: Without distinction, Mongol chiefs and the various princes all slightly disturb the people; resentment returns upon Your Majesty—this is what Your Majesty ought to ponder deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol chiefs and princes alike will harass the people in small ways, and resentment will fall on Your Majesty—that is what you must ponder deeply.

sentences.zh: 與其以長驅疲憊之兵入宣、大，孰若留精銳有餘之力取山海。

translations.literal: Rather than leading weary troops on a long drive into Xuan and Da, is it not better to keep elite strength in reserve and take Shanhai?
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep your elite strength in reserve and take Shanhai than to drive exhausted troops deep into Xuan and Da.

sentences.zh: 臣等明知失上旨，但既見及此，不容箝口也。」

translations.literal: We your servants clearly know we miss Your Majesty's intent, but having seen this, we cannot seal our mouths."
translations.idiomatic: We know we go against your intent, but having seen this much we cannot hold our tongues."

sentences.zh: 是時上已決用兵於宣、大，五月，上駐歸化城，召完我等計事。

translations.literal: At that time the sovereign had already decided to use force at Xuan and Da; in the fifth month he halted at Guihua city and summoned Wanwo and the others to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had already decided on war at Xuan and Da; in the fifth month he halted at Guihua and summoned Wanwo and the others to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 完我等疏論機宜，語詳文程傳。

translations.literal: Wanwo and the others memorialized on strategic points; the language is given in full in Wencheng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo and the others memorialized on strategy; the full text appears in Wencheng's biography.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上諭蒙古諸部及諸貝勒申軍律，蓋採完我等前疏所陳也。

translations.literal: The next day the sovereign instructed the Mongol tribes and the various princes to enforce military discipline—largely adopting what Wanwo and the others had set forth in their earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor instructed the Mongol tribes and princes to enforce military discipline, largely adopting Wanwo's earlier counsel.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，完我疏言：「近日朝鮮交益疏，南朝和未定，沈城不可以常都，兵事不可以久緩，機會不可以再失。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Wanwo memorialized: "Recently relations with Korea grow ever more distant, peace with the Southern Court is unsettled, Mukden cannot long remain the regular capital, military affairs cannot long be delayed, and opportunity cannot be lost again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 7 Wanwo memorialized: "Lately ties with Korea grow strained, peace with the Ming is unsettled, Mukden cannot long remain the capital, war cannot wait, and opportunity will not come twice.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖屢敗，何為而帝？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han was repeatedly defeated—why did he become emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han was beaten again and again—why did he become emperor?

sentences.zh: 項羽橫行天下，何為而亡？

translations.literal: Xiang Yu ranged across the realm—why did he perish?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu swept the realm—why did he fall?

sentences.zh: 袁紹擁河北之眾，何為而敗？

translations.literal: Yuan Shao held the masses of Hebei—why was he defeated?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao held all Hebei—why was he broken?

sentences.zh: 昭烈屢遘困難，何為而終霸？

translations.literal: Zhaolie repeatedly encountered hardship—why did he in the end dominate?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei met setback after setback—why did he still rise to hegemony?

sentences.zh: 無他，能用謀不能用謀，能乘機不能乘機而已。

translations.literal: There is no other reason: whether one can use stratagem or cannot, whether one can seize opportunity or cannot—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The difference is only this: using strategy or not, seizing opportunity or not.

sentences.zh: 夫天下大器也，可以智取，不可以力爭。

translations.literal: The realm is a great vessel—it may be taken by wit, not fought for by force.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is a great vessel—won by wit, not by brute force.

sentences.zh: 臣請以棋喻，能者戰守攻取，素熟於胸中，百局而百不負。

translations.literal: Your servant would use the game of go as analogy: the adept at defense, attack, and seizure has it all familiar in his breast—a hundred boards and not one lost.
translations.idiomatic: I would compare it to go: a master keeps attack and defense in his breast and wins a hundred games in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 至於取天下，是何等事，而可以草草僥倖耶？

translations.literal: As for taking the realm—what sort of affair is that, that one could treat it with careless luck?
translations.idiomatic: Winning the realm is no trifle—how can one trust to careless luck?

sentences.zh: 自古君臣相需，先帝時，達拉哈轄五大臣，知有上不知有人，知有國不知有家，故先帝以數十人起，克成大業。

translations.literal: Since antiquity ruler and minister have needed each other. In the Former Emperor's time, the Five Great Ministers under Dalahani knew the sovereign but knew no private persons, knew the state but knew no private families—thus the Former Emperor rose with dozens of men and accomplished the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister have always needed each other. Under the Former Emperor, the Five Great Ministers knew only the throne, not private ties; only the state, not private families—so he rose with a handful of men and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 上今環觀國中，如五大臣者有幾人耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty now surveys the state—how many men like the Five Great Ministers are there?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty looks about the court—how many men equal the Five Great Ministers?

sentences.zh: 每侍上治事，不聞諫諍，但有唯阿；

translations.literal: Whenever they attend Your Majesty in governing affairs, one hears no remonstrance, only yes-men;
translations.idiomatic: When they attend you in council, one hears no remonstrance—only flattery;

sentences.zh: 惟務苟且，不肯任勞怨。

translations.literal: They care only for muddling through and will not bear toil and blame.
translations.idiomatic: they seek only easy expedients and shun labor and blame.

sentences.zh: 於國何利？

translations.literal: What benefit to the state?
translations.idiomatic: What good does that do the state?

sentences.zh: 於上何益？

translations.literal: What profit to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: What good does it do you?

sentences.zh: 釣餌激勸，振刷轉移，臣望上於旦暮間也。

translations.literal: With bait to hook and stir, with a shake to brush and shift—I look to Your Majesty between morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Set hooks to lure them, shake the court to stir them—I beg Your Majesty to act between dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：'騏驥之局促，不如駑馬之安步；

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'A Qiji stallion's cramped steps cannot match a draft horse's steady pace;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'A Qiji's cramped stride cannot match a draft horse's steady walk;

sentences.zh: 孟賁之狐疑，不如庸夫之必至；

translations.literal: Meng Ben's hesitation cannot match a commoner's sure arrival;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ben's hesitation cannot match a common man's sure arrival;

sentences.zh: 雖有堯、舜之智，吟而不言，不如喑啞之指揮。

translations.literal: Though one had the wisdom of Yao and Shun, to chant and not speak cannot match a mute's signaling.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun's wisdom, chanted but never spoken, cannot match a mute's gestures.

sentences.zh: '此言貴能行之。

translations.literal: This speaks of valuing the ability to act.'
translations.idiomatic: That is praise for doing, not merely knowing.'

sentences.zh: 臣謹昧死上言，惟上裁擇。」

translations.literal: Your servant ventures death to speak upward; may Your Majesty judge and choose."
translations.idiomatic: I risk my life to speak; may Your Majesty judge and choose."

sentences.zh: 完我他所獻替，如論譯書，謂：「自金史外，當兼譯孝經、學、庸、論、孟、通鑑諸籍。」

translations.literal: Wanwo's other proposed reforms, such as on translating books, held: "Apart from the Jin History, one should also translate the Classic of Filial Piety, Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Analects, Mencius, Comprehensive Mirror, and such works."
translations.idiomatic: Among Wanwo's other proposals, on translation he argued: "Besides the Jin History, translate the Classic of Filial Piety, Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Analects, Mencius, the Comprehensive Mirror, and the like."

sentences.zh: 論試士，謂：「我國貪惰之俗，牢不可破，不當祗以筆舌取人，試前宜刷陋習，試後宜察素行。

translations.literal: On examining scholars he held: "Our state's greed and sloth are deeply rooted; one must not choose men by brush and tongue alone—before the examination scrub away vulgar habits, after it inspect their ordinary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On the civil examinations he wrote: "Greed and sloth run too deep here to break by pen alone—purge bad habits before the exam and inspect conduct afterward.

sentences.zh: 且六部中，滿、漢官吏及大凌河將備，當悉令入試，既可覘此等人才調，且令此等人皆自科目出，庶同貴此途不相冰炭也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, among the Six Ministries, Manchu and Han officials and Dalinghe generals-in-waiting should all be made to enter the examinations—thus one may observe the caliber of such men, and let them all emerge through the civil-service route so they may equally honor this path and not be ice and fire to one another."
translations.idiomatic: Every Manchu and Han officer in the Six Ministries and every Dalinghe garrison commander should sit the exams too—so you can gauge their talent and so all rise by the same road, not as sworn enemies."

sentences.zh: 論六部治事，謂：「六部本循明製，漢承政皆墨守大明會典，宜參酌彼此，殫心竭思，就今日規模，別立會典。

translations.literal: On the Six Ministries' handling of affairs he held: "The Six Ministries originally follow the Ming system; Han administrators all cling to the Great Ming Statutes—one should weigh both sides, exhaust heart and thought, and on today's scale separately establish a new code.
translations.idiomatic: On the Six Ministries he urged: "They still follow Ming forms; Han staff cling to the Great Ming Statutes—weigh both traditions, think hard, and draft a new code for our own day.

sentences.zh: 務去因循之習，漸就中國之制度，庶異日既得中原，不至於自擾。

translations.literal: Strive to remove routinist habits, gradually approach China's institutions, so that when one day the Central Plains are gained, one will not throw oneself into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shake off inertia, move toward Chinese institutions, and when we hold the Central Plains we will not founder in our own confusion.

sentences.zh: 昔漢繼秦而王，蕭何任造律，叔孫通任制禮。

translations.literal: Of old Han succeeded Qin as king; Xiao He was charged with making laws, Shusun Tong with making rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Han succeeded Qin, Xiao He made the laws and Shusun Tong the rites.

sentences.zh: 彼猶是人也，前無所因，尚能造律制禮；

translations.literal: They were yet men; with nothing before to follow, they could still make laws and rites;
translations.idiomatic: They were only men, with no precedent—yet they made laws and rites;

sentences.zh: 今既有成法，乃不能通其變，則又何也？

translations.literal: now when there are already established laws, yet one cannot penetrate their changes—then what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: now that we have models before us, why can we not adapt them?

sentences.zh: 六部漢承政宜人置一通事，上亦宜以譯者侍左右，俾時召對，毋使以不通滿語自諉。」

translations.literal: In the Six Ministries each Han administrator should have an interpreter placed; Your Majesty too should have translators attend at your side, so they may be summoned for audience and not excuse themselves for not knowing Manchu."
translations.idiomatic: Place an interpreter with each Han administrator in the Six Ministries, and keep translators at your side so you can summon them—let no one plead ignorance of Manchu."

sentences.zh: 完我疏屢上，上每採其議。

translations.literal: Wanwo's memorials were repeatedly submitted; each time the sovereign adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo memorialized again and again, and the sovereign adopted his counsel each time.

sentences.zh: 完我又嘗疏薦李率泰、陳錦，皆至大用。

translations.literal: Wanwo also once memorialized recommending Li Shuaitai and Chen Jin, both of whom rose to great employment.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Li Shuaitai and Chen Jin, both of whom rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 惟論用兵，力主自寧、錦直攻山海，不原出宣、大；

translations.literal: Only on using troops he strongly held that one should attack Shanhai directly from Ning and Jin, and opposed advancing from Xuan and Da;
translations.idiomatic: On military affairs alone he insisted on striking Shanhai Pass from Ningyuan and Jinzhou, not on a drive through Xuan and Da;

sentences.zh: 孔有德、耿仲明降時，完我疏言當收其兵入烏真超哈，繼又言有德、仲明暴戾無才，其兵多礦徒，食盡且為盜：皆未當上旨。

translations.literal: When Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming submitted, Wanwo memorialized that their troops should be taken into the Ujen Cooha; later he also said Youde and Zhongming were violent and without talent, their troops mostly miners, who when grain ran out would become bandits: none of this suited the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming surrendered, Wanwo urged absorbing their troops into the Ujen Cooha; later he called them brutal and talentless, their men mostly miners who would turn bandit when provisions failed—none of which pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，范文程上言薦舉太濫，舉主雖不連坐，亦當議罰。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year Fan Wencheng memorialized that recommendations were too promiscuous; though the recommender might not be punished by association, he should still be subject to discussion and penalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 9 Fan Wencheng argued that patronage had grown too loose; even without joint punishment, recommenders should face review and penalty.

sentences.zh: 完我亦疏請功罪皆當並議，略言：「上令官民皆得薦舉，本欲得才以任事，乃無知者假此幸進，兩部已四五十人，其濫可見。

translations.literal: Wanwo also memorialized that merit and fault should both be discussed together, saying in brief: "Your Majesty ordered that officials and commoners alike might recommend, originally intending to gain talent for employment—yet the ignorant use this to advance by luck; the two ministries already have forty or fifty men, and how promiscuous this is may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo asked that merit and fault be judged together, writing in brief: "You opened recommendation to officials and commoners to gain talent—but the ignorant seize the chance; the two ministries already hold forty or fifty such men, which shows how loose it has become.

sentences.zh: 當行連坐法，所舉得人，舉主同其賞；

translations.literal: One should enforce the law of linked responsibility: if what one recommends gains a man, the recommender shares his reward;
translations.idiomatic: Enforce joint liability: if a nominee succeeds, the recommender shares the reward;

sentences.zh: 所舉失人，舉主同其罪；

translations.literal: if what one recommends loses a man, the recommender shares his guilt;
translations.idiomatic: if the nominee fails, the recommender shares the blame;

sentences.zh: 如有末路改節，許舉主自陳，貸其罪。

translations.literal: if there is late-course change of loyalty, let the recommender confess himself and remit his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: if a man turns traitor at the end, let the recommender confess and be spared.

sentences.zh: 如採此法，臣度不三日，請罷舉者十當八九；

translations.literal: If this law is adopted, your servant estimates that within three days those begging to be excused from recommending will be eight or nine in ten;
translations.idiomatic: Adopt this, and within three days nine in ten will withdraw their nominations;

sentences.zh: 其有留者，不問皆真才矣。」

translations.literal: those who remain—all without asking are true talent."
translations.idiomatic: those who remain will be true talent indeed."

sentences.zh: 上並嘉納。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both memorials.

sentences.zh: 完我久預機務，遇事敢言，累進世職二等甲喇章京，襲六次，賜莊田、奴僕，上駸駸倚任，顧喜酒縱博。

translations.literal: Wanwo long handled confidential affairs, spoke boldly when matters arose, was repeatedly promoted two grades in hereditary jalan rank, inherited six times, granted estate fields and slaves; the sovereign leaned on him ever more, yet he loved wine and indulged in gambling.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo long handled state secrets and spoke his mind; he was twice promoted in hereditary jalan rank, inherited six times, and received estates and slaves. The throne relied on him ever more, yet he loved wine and dice.

sentences.zh: 初從上伐明，命助守永平，以博為禮部參政李伯龍及游擊佟整所劾，上為誡諭，宥之。

translations.literal: At first on the campaign against Ming he was ordered to assist in holding Yongping; for gambling he was impeached by Li Bolong, Vice Minister of Rites, and Tong Zheng, Guerrilla Officer; the sovereign admonished him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the first Ming campaign he was ordered to help hold Yongping; Li Bolong, Vice Minister of Rites, and Guerrilla Tong Zheng impeached him for gambling; the emperor admonished him and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，复坐與大凌河降將甲喇章京劉士英博，為士英奴所訐，削​​世職，盡奪所賜，仍令給事薩哈廉家。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year he again sat in gambling with Liu Shiying, a jalan rank from Dalinghe who had submitted; impeached by Shiying's slave, his hereditary rank was stripped, all gifts seized, and he was still ordered to serve in Sahalian's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 10 he gambled again with Liu Shiying, a surrendered Dalinghe jalan; Shiying's slave denounced him, his hereditary rank was stripped, his gifts seized, and he was sent back to Sahalian's household.

sentences.zh: 是年改元崇德，以文館為內三院，希福、文程、承先皆為大學士，完我以罪廢，不得與。

translations.literal: That year the reign title changed to Chongde; the Literary Bureau became the Inner Three Courts; Xifu, Wencheng, and Chengxian all became Grand Secretaries—Wanwo, dismissed for crime, was not included.
translations.idiomatic: That year the era name became Chongde; the Literary Bureau became the Inner Three Courts. Xifu, Wencheng, and Chengxian became Grand Secretaries—Wanwo, disgraced, was left out.

sentences.zh: 及世祖定鼎京師，起完我為學士。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor established the capital at Beijing, Wanwo was raised as academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital at Beijing, Wanwo was restored as an academician.

sentences.zh: 順治二年五月，授內弘文院大學士，充明史總裁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Inner Hongwen Court and made chief compiler of the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shunzhi 2 he became Grand Secretary of the Inner Hongwen Court and chief compiler of the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 是年及三年、六年，並充會試總裁。

translations.literal: That year and in the third and sixth years he served repeatedly as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: That year and again in years 3 and 6 he served as chief metropolitan examiner.

sentences.zh: 又命監修太宗實錄，譯三國志、洪武寶訓諸書，复授二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of Taizong, translated the Records of the Three Kingdoms, Precious Instructions of the Hongwu Reign, and other books, and was again granted a second-grade adaha gūwa.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Veritable Records of Taizong, translated the Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Hongwu Precious Instructions, and other works, and was again granted a second-grade adaha gūwa.

sentences.zh: 八年閏二月，大學士剛林、祁充格得罪，完我以知睿親王改太祖實錄未啟奏，當奪職，鄭親王濟爾哈朗等覆讞，以為無罪，得免。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the eighth year Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were punished; Wanwo should have lost his post for knowing the Prince of Rui had altered the Veritable Records of Taizu without memorializing—Prince of Zheng Jirhalang and others reviewed the case and held him guiltless, so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of year 8 Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge fell; Wanwo should have been dismissed for knowing the Prince of Rui had altered Taizu's Veritable Records without reporting it—Prince of Zheng Jirhalang and others reviewed the case and acquitted him.

sentences.zh: 三月，調內國史院大學士，命班位祿秩從滿洲大學士例。

translations.literal: In the third month he was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Inner Historiography Court, with order that his rank, precedence, and salary follow the Manchu grand secretaries' example.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he moved to Grand Secretary of the Inner Historiography Court, with rank, precedence, and salary equal to the Manchu grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 尋授議政大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Deliberating Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named a Deliberating Minister.

sentences.zh: 十一年三月，疏劾大學士陳名夏結黨懷姦，臚舉名夏塗抹票擬稿簿，刪改諭旨，庇護同黨，縱子掖臣為害鄉里，凡七事；

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year he memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia for forming factions and harboring treachery, listing seven matters including Mingxia's smearing the draft proposal ledger, deleting and altering edicts, shielding partisans, and letting his son support clerks to harm the neighborhood;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 11 he impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia for faction and treachery, citing seven counts: tampering with draft memorials, altering edicts, shielding allies, letting his son's clients terrorize their home district, and more;

sentences.zh: 復言：「從古奸臣賊子，黨不成則計不行。

translations.literal: He added: "Since antiquity treacherous ministers and wicked sons—if the faction does not form, the scheme cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Since antiquity, traitors and villains cannot act until their faction is formed.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 無真才，無實事，無顯功，故必結黨為之虛譽。

translations.literal: Without real talent, without real deeds, without manifest merit, they must form factions to build them false fame.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking talent, deeds, and merit, they must form cliques to manufacture reputation.

sentences.zh: 欲黨之成，附己者雖惡必護，異己者雖善必仇，行之久而入黨者多。

translations.literal: To make the faction succeed: those who attach to oneself, though evil, must be shielded; those unlike oneself, though good, must be hated—practiced long, those entering the faction grow many.
translations.idiomatic: To build a faction they shield their own, however vile, and hate outsiders, however worthy—given time, the clique swells.

sentences.zh: 若非審察鄉評輿論，按其行事，則黨固莫可破矣。

translations.literal: Unless one closely examines village appraisals and public opinion and judges by their conduct, the faction solidly cannot be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you weigh local reputation and judge by deeds, the clique cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 臣竊自念，壯年孟浪疏庸，辜負先帝，一廢十年。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects privately: in my prime I was reckless, shallow, and mediocre and failed the Former Emperor—dismissed once for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect: in my prime I was rash and shallow and failed the Former Emperor—I was cast aside for ten years.

sentences.zh: 皇上定鼎，始得隨入禁地，謹守臣職，又復十年，忍性緘口。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty fixed the tripod-capital I could at last follow into the forbidden precincts, strictly kept minister's duty, again ten years, bearing my nature and sealing my mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty fixed the capital I entered the inner court, kept my post in silence another ten years, biting back my nature.

sentences.zh: 然愚直性生，遇事勃發，埋輪補牘，雖不敢行；

translations.literal: Yet blunt honesty is born in my nature; when matters arise I flare up—burying-the-wheel and patching-the-records bold remonstrance I dare not practice;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am blunt by nature and flare when wrong is done—I dare not play the martyr who blocks the wheel or patches the palace gate;

sentences.zh: 若夫附黨營私以圖富貴，臣寧死不為也。

translations.literal: but as for attaching to factions to seek private gain and plot wealth and rank, your servant would rather die than do it.
translations.idiomatic: but to join a faction for private gain I would rather die.

sentences.zh: 皇上不以臣衰老，列諸滿大臣；

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not regard your servant as aged and listed him among the Manchu grand ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not dismiss me for age but ranked me among the Manchu grand ministers;

sentences.zh: 聖壽召入深宮，親賜御酒。

translations.literal: at the imperial birthday summoned him into the deep palace and personally bestowed imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: on your birthday you summoned me to the inner palace and poured imperial wine yourself.

sentences.zh: 臣非土木，敢不盡​​心力圖報。

translations.literal: Your servant is no timber or earth—how dare he not exhaust heart and strength to repay?
translations.idiomatic: I am not wood or stone—how could I not give you my utmost?

sentences.zh: 名夏姦亂日甚，黨局日成。

translations.literal: Mingxia's treachery grew daily worse, the faction daily formed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia's treachery worsened daily; his faction hardened daily.

sentences.zh: 人鑑張煊而莫敢言，臣不憚舍殘軀以報聖主。」

translations.literal: Men took Zhang Xuan as a mirror yet dared not speak; your servant does not fear leaving this broken body to repay the sage sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: All saw Zhang Xuan's fate and held their tongues; I do not fear this broken body if it serves my lord."

sentences.zh: 名夏坐是譴死。

translations.literal: Mingxia on this account was condemned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia was condemned on these grounds and executed.

sentences.zh: 八月，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was made Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年九月，以老乞休，溫諭命致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year, citing age he begged retirement; a warm edict ordered him to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 15 he begged leave on account of age; a gracious edict let him retire.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年正月，聖祖念完我事太宗﹑世祖有勞，命官一子為學士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor, recalling Wanwo's service to Taizong and Shizu, ordered one son appointed academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 1 the Sacred Ancestor, remembering Wanwo's service to Taizong and Shizu, appointed one son an academician.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，卒，諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year he died; posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 4 he died; his posthumous name was Wenyi (Cultivated and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 雍正六年七月，世宗命錄完我子孫，得曾孫蘭，以驍騎校待缺，賜宅，予白金五百。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yongzheng the Shizong ordered Wanwo's descendants recorded; a great-grandson Lan was found, given a vacant post as valiant cavalry captain, granted a residence, and awarded five hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongzheng 6 the Shizong ordered Wanwo's line recorded; a great-grandson Lan was found, given a vacant valiant-cavalry captaincy, a house, and five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 鮑承先，山西應州人。

translations.literal: Bao Chengxian was a man of Yingzhou, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chengxian was from Yingzhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆間，積官至參將。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era of Ming he rose by accumulation to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he rose through the ranks to brigadier general.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年，從總兵賀世賢、李秉誠守瀋陽城，遷開原東路統領新勇營副將，城守如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he followed Generals He Shixian and Li Bingcheng in defending Shenyang city; he was transferred to deputy commander of the New Braves Battalion commanding the eastern route of Kaiyuan, defending the city as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 1 he followed Generals He Shixian and Li Bingcheng in defending Shenyang, then became deputy commander of the New Braves on Kaiyuan's eastern route, still holding the walls.

sentences.zh: 經略熊廷弼疏請獎勵諸將，承先預焉，加都督僉事銜。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xiong Tingbi memorialized to reward the generals—Chengxian was among them—and he received the brevet rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xiong Tingbi memorialized to reward the generals; Chengxian was included and received the brevet rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 是歲為天命五年。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Tianming.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Tianming 5.

sentences.zh: 太祖已克開原，乃自懿路、蒲河二路進兵向瀋陽。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor had already taken Kaiyuan and advanced from the Yilu and Puhe routes toward Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had taken Kaiyuan and advanced on Shenyang by the Yilu and Puhe routes.

sentences.zh: 承先偕世賢、秉誠出城，分汛駐守，見太祖兵至，皆不戰退。

translations.literal: Chengxian with Shixian and Bingcheng left the city and garrisoned at separate defense posts; seeing the Taizu army arrive, all withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian, Shixian, and Bingcheng left the city to man outposts; when Taizu's army appeared, all withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 上令左翼兵逐承先等，迫瀋陽城北，斬百餘級而去。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered the Left Wing to pursue Chengxian and the others, pressing to north of Shenyang, cutting down more than a hundred heads before departing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Left Wing to pursue them to north of Shenyang, took more than a hundred heads, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，上克瀋陽、遼陽，世賢戰死，承先退保廣寧。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year the sovereign took Shenyang and Liaoyang; Shixian died in battle, Chengxian withdrew to defend Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 7 the emperor took Shenyang and Liaoyang; Shixian fell in battle and Chengxian fell back on Guangning.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，克西平堡，承先從秉誠及總兵劉渠、祁秉忠等自廣寧赴援，渠、秉忠戰死，承先與秉誠敗走，全軍盡殪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Xiping Fort was taken; Chengxian followed Bingcheng and Generals Liu Qu, Qi Bingzhong, and others from Guangning to the relief; Qu and Bingzhong died in battle, Chengxian and Bingcheng fled in defeat, the entire army destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 8 Xiping Fort fell; Chengxian marched from Guangning with Bingcheng, Liu Qu, Qi Bingzhong, and others to relieve it; Qu and Bingzhong were killed, Chengxian and Bingcheng fled, and the whole force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王化貞棄廣寧走入關，游擊孫得功等以廣寧降。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen abandoned Guangning and fled into the passes; Guerrilla Sun Degong and others submitted Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen abandoned Guangning and fled inside the passes; Guerrilla Sun Degong and others surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 承先竄匿數日，從眾出降，仍授副將。

translations.literal: Chengxian hid for several days, then followed the crowd out to submit and was again appointed deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian hid several days, then came out with the rest to surrender and was again made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，太宗自將伐明，自龍井關入邊，承先從鄭親王濟爾哈朗略馬蘭峪，屢敗明兵，承先以書招其守將來降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong the Taizong personally led a campaign against Ming, entering the frontier through Longjing Pass; Chengxian followed Prince of Zheng Jirhalang in raiding Malan Valley, repeatedly defeating Ming troops; Chengxian by letter summoned its defending general to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 Hong Taiji led the campaign against Ming through Longjing Pass; Chengxian followed Prince of Zheng Jirhalang in raiding Malan Valley, repeatedly routing Ming forces, and by letter induced its commander to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師進薄明都，承先复招降牧馬廠太監，獲其馬騾以濟師。
