translations.literal: The army advanced close to the Ming capital; Chengxian again induced the horse-pasture eunuch to submit and obtained his horses and mules to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed the Ming capital; Chengxian again won over the horse-pasture eunuch and took his horses and mules to supply the host.

sentences.zh: 明經略袁崇煥以二萬人自寧遠入援，屯廣渠門外，憑險設伏。

translations.literal: Ming Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan with twenty thousand men came from Ningyuan in relief, encamped outside Guangqu Gate, relying on terrain to set ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan marched twenty thousand men from Ningyuan to relieve the capital, camped outside Guangqu Gate, and used the terrain for ambush.

sentences.zh: 貝勒豪格督兵出其右，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: Prince Hoge directed troops out on their right flank; battle was repeatedly victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hoge struck their right wing and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 是時承先以寧完我薦直文館，翌日，上誡諸軍勿進攻，召承先及副將高鴻中授以秘計，使近陣獲明內監系所並坐，故相耳語，云：「今日撤兵乃上計也。

translations.literal: At that time Chengxian through Ning Wanwo's recommendation served in the Literary Bureau; the next day the sovereign warned the armies not to press the attack, summoned Chengxian and Deputy Commander Gao Hongzhong and gave them a secret plan—having them approach the formation, seize a Ming inner eunuch where he was bound, and sit together, deliberately whispering to each other, saying: "Today's withdrawal of troops is the superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian had entered the Literary Bureau on Wanwo's recommendation; the next day the emperor forbade a general assault, summoned Chengxian and Deputy Commander Gao Hongzhong, and gave them a secret ruse—seize a bound Ming eunuch near the lines, sit beside him, and whisper aloud: "Today's withdrawal is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 頃見上單騎向敵，有二人自敵中來，見上，語良久乃去。

translations.literal: Just now I saw the sovereign ride alone toward the enemy; two men came from the enemy, saw the sovereign, spoke long, then left.
translations.idiomatic: I just saw the emperor ride alone toward the enemy; two men came out, spoke with him at length, and left.

sentences.zh: 意袁經略有密約，此事可立就矣。」

translations.literal: I suppose Grand Coordinator Yuan has a secret pact—this affair can be accomplished at once."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan must have a secret pact—this can be settled at once."

sentences.zh: 內監楊某佯臥竊聽，越日，縱之歸，以告明帝，遂殺崇煥。

translations.literal: The inner eunuch surnamed Yang feigned sleep to eavesdrop; the next day they released him to return, and he told the Ming emperor—thus Chonghuan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yang pretended to sleep and listened; the next day they let him go; he told the Ming emperor, and Chonghuan was executed.

sentences.zh: 四年，師克永平，承先從，以書諭遷安諸紳硃堅台、卜文煥以城降，遂取灤州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the army took Yongping; Chengxian followed and by letter instructed the gentry of Qian'an Zhu Jiantai and Bu Wenhuan to submit the city, then took Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the army took Yongping; Chengxian followed and by letter persuaded the Qian'an gentry Zhu Jiantai and Bu Wenhuan to surrender, then took Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命承先與副將白格率鑲黃、鑲藍二旗兵守遷安，立台堡五，明兵來攻，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Chengxian with Deputy Commander Bai'e to lead the Bordered Yellow and Bordered Blue banners' troops to hold Qian'an, building five tower-forts; Ming troops came to attack and they fought them off by force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chengxian and Deputy Commander Bai'e to hold Qian'an with the Bordered Yellow and Bordered Blue banners, built five tower-forts, and beat back Ming attacks.

sentences.zh: 明監軍道張春、總兵祖大壽等合諸軍攻灤州，貝勒阿敏令承先以守遷安兵守永平。

translations.literal: Ming Superintendent Zhang Chun, General Zu Dashou, and others combined armies to attack Luanzhou; Prince Amin ordered Chengxian to take the Qian'an garrison to hold Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Superintendent Zhang Chun, Zu Dashou, and others besieged Luanzhou; Prince Amin sent Chengxian's Qian'an garrison to hold Yongping.

sentences.zh: 及灤州破，阿敏棄永平，率諸將出冷口，東還瀋陽。

translations.literal: When Luanzhou fell, Amin abandoned Yongping, led the generals out Cold Pass, and returned east to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Luanzhou fell, Amin abandoned Yongping, led the army out Cold Pass, and marched east to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 上命定諸將棄地罪，以承先、白格守遷安，完城退敵，釋弗問。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered penalties fixed for the generals who abandoned territory; because Chengxian and Bai'e held Qian'an, completed the walls, and repelled the enemy, they were released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fixed penalties for generals who abandoned ground; Chengxian and Bai'e, having held Qian'an, finished the walls, and repulsed the enemy, were excused.

sentences.zh: 五年，從攻大凌河，降翟家堡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the attack on Dalinghe and brought Zhujia Fort to submission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he joined the siege of Dalinghe and reduced Zhujia Fort.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，上詢文館諸臣，考各部啟心郎優絀以為黜陟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year the sovereign questioned the Literary Bureau ministers, examining the relative merit of each ministry's translating secretaries for promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 6 the emperor questioned the Literary Bureau, ranking each ministry's translating secretaries for promotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 承先與寧完我、范文程疏言：「當察其建言，或實心為國，或巧言塞責，以為去留。」

translations.literal: Chengxian with Ning Wanwo and Fan Wencheng memorialized: "One should examine their memorialized words—whether wholehearted for the state or artful words to block responsibility—as the basis for retention or dismissal."
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian, Wanwo, and Wencheng memorialized: "Judge them by what they say—whether they serve the state in earnest or fob off duty with clever words—and keep or dismiss them accordingly."

sentences.zh: 七年五月，孔有德、耿仲明來降，泊舟鎮江。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming came to surrender, anchoring their ships at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 7, Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming surrendered and moored their fleet at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 承先疏言：「用舟師攻明宜急進，否則，明亦廣練舟師以御，即不能為功。」

translations.literal: Chengxian memorialized: "In attacking Ming with a naval force one ought to press forward quickly; otherwise Ming too will broadly drill naval forces to defend, and then success cannot be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian memorialized: "Strike Ming by sea now, before they build a fleet to meet us—delay, and the chance is lost."

sentences.zh: 七月，既克旅順，承先復請移鎮江諸艦泊蓋州，收旁近諸島，以仁義撫其人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, once Lüshun had been taken, Chengxian again asked to move the Zhenjiang ships to moor at Gaizhou, gather the nearby islands, and soothe their people with benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That July, after Lüshun fell, he urged moving the Zhenjiang squadron to Gaizhou, bringing in the outlying islands and winning their people with clemency.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，上伐明大同，明總督張宗衡、總兵曹文詔等遣承先子韜齎書請和。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year the sovereign campaigned against Ming at Datong; Ming Governor Zhang Zongheng, General Cao Wenzhao, and others sent Chengxian's son Tao bearing a letter to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 8 the emperor marched on Ming Datong; Ming Governor Zhang Zongheng and General Cao Wenzhao sent Chengxian's son Tao with a letter seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 初，承先降，明人執韜系應州獄，至是出之，使以書來，山行，遇土謝圖濟農兵，奪其騎，斫韜及從者，皆死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chengxian surrendered, Ming men seized Tao and bound him in Yingzhou prison; now they released him and sent him with the letter. Traveling by mountain path, he met Tuxietu Jinong troops, who seized his horse, hacked Tao and his attendants—all died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengxian had first defected, the Ming had held Tao in Yingzhou jail; now they freed him to carry the letter. On the mountain road he ran into Tuxietu Jinong's men, who took his horse and cut down Tao and his escort—all were left for dead.

sentences.zh: 兵去，韜復甦。

translations.literal: The soldiers departed; Tao revived.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers had gone, Tao came to.

sentences.zh: 有馮國珍者，送韜至貝勒代善營，令與承先相見，遂使入謁上。

translations.literal: One Feng Guozhen conveyed Tao to Prince Daishan's camp, had him meet Chengxian, and then sent him in to audience with the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Feng Guozhen brought Tao to Prince Daishan's camp, reunited him with Chengxian, and had him presented to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上見韜創甚，留軍中，遣國珍齎書還。

translations.literal: The sovereign saw Tao's wounds were severe, kept him in the army, and sent Guozhen back bearing the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tao badly wounded, the emperor kept him with the army and sent Guozhen back with the reply.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，承先疏言：「臣竊見元帥孔有德、總兵耿仲明為其屬員請敕，上許其自行給劄。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Chengxian memorialized: "Your servant has observed that Marshal Kong Youde and General Geng Zhongming, on behalf of their subordinates, requested patents; the sovereign permitted them to issue commissions on their own.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9 Chengxian wrote: "I see Marshal Kong Youde and General Geng Zhongming were allowed to issue patents to their own men at their discretion.

sentences.zh: 帝王開國，首重名器，上下之分，自有定禮。

translations.literal: When emperors and kings found a state, they first esteem titular regalia; the distinction of superior and inferior has its fixed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Founding a dynasty begins with honoring the insignia of rank—high and low have their proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 倘欲加意招徠遠人，可諭吏部奏請給劄，使恩出上裁。」

translations.literal: If one wishes especially to win over men from afar, one may instruct the Board of Personnel to memorialize requesting issuance of commissions, so that grace issues from the sovereign's decision."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to court distant allies warmly, have the Board of Personnel petition to issue patents, so favor comes from your own hand."

sentences.zh: 上不謂然，諭曰：「元帥率眾航海遠來，厥功匪小。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not agree and instructed: "The marshal led his multitude across the sea from afar—the achievement is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disagreed and said: "The marshal brought his men by sea from far away—that is no small service.

sentences.zh: 任賢勿貳，載在虞書。

translations.literal: The Book of Yu records, "Employ the worthy without wavering."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu says, "Appoint the worthy and do not doubt them."

sentences.zh: 朕推誠待下，前旨已行，豈可食言？

translations.literal: I treat my subordinates with open sincerity; the earlier order has already gone forth—how can I eat my words?
translations.idiomatic: I deal with my men in good faith; my word is already given—would you have me break it?

sentences.zh: 承先敗走乞降，今尚列諸功臣，給敕恩養。

translations.literal: Chengxian fled in defeat and begged to surrender, yet today he still ranks among the meritorious ministers and receives patents and sustaining grace.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian himself fled and sued for mercy—yet he still stands among my great ministers, favored with patents and stipends.

sentences.zh: 豈遠來歸順諸將吏反謂無功？

translations.literal: How could the generals and officials who came from afar to submit be said to have no achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Shall those who crossed the sea to join me be told they have done nothing?

sentences.zh: 朕此言亦非責承先也，彼以誠入告，朕亦以誠開示之耳。」

translations.literal: My words are also not to blame Chengxian; he advised with sincerity, and I likewise clarify matters with sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean this as rebuke to you, Chengxian—you spoke in earnest, and I answer in earnest."

sentences.zh: 旋自察哈爾得元傳國璽，承先請命工部製璽函，卜吉日，躬率群臣郊迎入宮，仍以得璽敕示滿﹑漢、蒙古，上從之。

translations.literal: Soon the Yuan dynastic seal was obtained from the Chahar; Chengxian asked the Board of Works to make a casket for the seal, chose an auspicious day, and in person led the ministers in suburban welcome to bring it into the palace; he also memorialized that an edict announce the gaining of the seal to Manchu, Han, and Mongol—the sovereign assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan imperial seal was taken from the Chahar, Chengxian had the Board of Works fashion a reliquary, chose a lucky day, and led the court in a suburban ceremony to carry it into the palace; he also urged an edict to proclaim the seal to Manchus, Han, and Mongols alike—and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既，承先與文館諸臣隨諸貝勒文武將吏請上尊號。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chengxian with the Literary Bureau ministers followed the princes, civil and military officers, and generals in requesting the sovereign assume an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chengxian and the Literary Bureau joined the princes, officials, and generals in asking the emperor to take a regnal title.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，改文館為內三院，承先授內秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde the Literary Bureau was changed to the Inner Three Courts; Chengxian was appointed Grand Secretary of the Inner Secretariat Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde the Literary Bureau became the Inner Three Courts, and Chengxian became Grand Secretary of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，改吏部右參政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Vice Commissioner of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made Right Vice Commissioner of the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年，漢軍八旗制定，承先隸正紅旗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Eight Banners of the Han Army were fixed; Chengxian was registered in the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Han Army Eight Banners were organized, and Chengxian was placed in the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 五年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗等圍明錦州，令防守袞塔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince of Zheng Jirhalang and others in besieging Ming Jinzhou and was ordered to defend Guntai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he joined Prince Zheng Jirhalang in the siege of Jinzhou and was posted to defend Guntai.

sentences.zh: 耕時明兵傷我農民，承先退避不及援，坐論死，上宥之。

translations.literal: During plowing season Ming troops wounded our farmers; Chengxian withdrew and could not reach them in time to relieve—on conviction the penalty was death, but the sovereign pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: During the harvest Ming raiders struck our peasants; Chengxian fell back too late to help and was sentenced to death—the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 尋以病解任。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，世祖定鼎燕京，承先從入關，賜銀幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the Shizu emperor fixed the capital at Yanjing; Chengxian followed in entering the Pass and was gifted silver, coins, and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi the Shunzhi Emperor made Yanjing his capital; Chengxian entered the Pass with him and received silver, coins, and horses.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，命大學士范文程視含斂。

translations.literal: In the second year he died; the Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng was ordered to oversee placing the jade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 2; Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng was charged with his funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 子敬，授三等阿思哈尼哈番，官河北總兵。

translations.literal: His son Jing was granted third-rank ashan i hafan and served as Commander-in-chief of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing received third-rank ashan i hafan and became Commander-in-chief of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，剿流賊郝搖旗，縱不追，坐降四級。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, in suppressing the roving bandit Hao Yaoqi, he let him go without pursuit—on conviction he was demoted four grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 4, chasing the rebel Hao Yaoqi, he failed to pursue and was demoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 復起為大同總兵。

translations.literal: He was again raised and made Commander-in-chief of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as Commander-in-chief of Datong.

sentences.zh: 入為鑾儀衛鑾儀使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Master of Ceremonies of the Imperial Procession Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Master of Ceremonies in the Imperial Procession Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 高鴻中與承先同直文館。

translations.literal: Gao Hongzhong served in the same Literary Bureau shift as Chengxian.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hongzhong shared a shift with Chengxian in the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 克永平四城，承先助守遷安，而令鴻中助守灤州，蓋使文館諸臣習武事。

translations.literal: When the four cities of Yongping were taken, Chengxian assisted in holding Qian'an while Hongzhong was ordered to assist in holding Luanzhou—so that the Literary Bureau ministers might practice military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongping quadrant fell, Chengxian helped hold Qian'an and Hongzhong Luanzhou—training the Literary Bureau in war.

sentences.zh: 旋以鴻中領甲喇額真。

translations.literal: Soon Hongzhong was made to lead as jiala ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhong was soon made a jiala ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，設六部，授刑部承政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong the Six Ministries were established; he was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 5 the Six Ministries were set up, and he became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏論刑部事當釐正者四，謂：「諸臣敕書賜免死，有罪宜先去'免死'字，更有罪乃追敕書，不當遽議削奪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized on four matters of the Board of Punishments needing correction, saying: "When ministers' patent letters grant exemption from death, on guilt one should first remove the words 'exemption from death'; only on further guilt should the patent be recalled—not rashly debate confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he listed four reforms for the Board of Punishments: "Patents that grant ministers immunity from death should first have that immunity struck on a first offense; only repeat offenders forfeit the patent—not instant confiscation.

sentences.zh: 諸臣坐罪輒罰鍰，非古制；

translations.literal: When ministers are convicted they are immediately fined in money—this is not the ancient system;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers today are fined at once for any crime—that is not ancient practice;

sentences.zh: 且罰鍰視職崇庳，不問罪輕重，宜有定程。

translations.literal: moreover fines are set by rank high or low without regard to gravity of crime—there ought to be fixed scales.
translations.idiomatic: and fines follow rank, not guilt—there should be fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 滿民有罪待讞，所屬牛錄若家主，輒與讞獄吏同坐，辨論紛擾，擬嚴定以罪，著為令。

translations.literal: When Manchu people guilty await judgment, their niru or household head constantly sits with the judging officials—disputation and turmoil; he proposed sternly fixing penalties and making them statute.
translations.idiomatic: When a Manchu awaits trial, his niru chief or master sits in court with the judge, breeding chaos—he urged fixed penalties and a written law.

sentences.zh: 刑曹讞獄，滿、漢官會讞，民不便，宜令滿官主滿民獄訟，漢官主漢民獄訟。」

translations.literal: The punishment office jointly judges cases with Manchu and Han officials together—unconvenient for the people; Manchu officials should preside over Manchu litigation, Han officials over Han litigation."
translations.idiomatic: Mixed Manchu and Han benches strain litigants—let Manchu judges hear Manchu cases and Han judges hear Han cases."

sentences.zh: 旋复條奏時政，上諭文館諸臣曰：「上書建言，固不可禁遏。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again memorialized item by item on current policy; the sovereign instructed the Literary Bureau ministers: "Memorializing with advice certainly cannot be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized again on policy. The emperor told the Literary Bureau: "Petitioning with advice must not be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 鴻中疏多言古人過失，昔元成吉思皇帝子察罕代以刀削檉柳為鞭，曰：'我國，父皇所定；

translations.literal: Hongzhong's memorials often spoke of ancients' faults. Formerly Genghis Khan's son Chaghan made a willow-tamarisk whip by shaving with a knife, saying: 'Our state my imperial father established;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhong's memorials often faulted the ancients. Genghis Khan's son Chaghan once carved a tamarisk whip with his knife and said: 'Our realm was my father's work;

sentences.zh: 此檉柳鞭，乃我所手創也。

translations.literal: this willow-tamarisk whip is what I myself created by hand.'
translations.idiomatic: this willow whip I carved with my own hand.'

sentences.zh: '其臣俄齊爾塞臣曰：'非先帝鳩工製此刀，則此檉柳豈能以指削，以齒齧耶？

translations.literal: His minister Okur Secen said: 'Had not the late emperor gathered labor to make this knife, could this willow be shaved with a finger or gnawed with teeth?
translations.idiomatic: His minister Okur Secen replied: 'Had the late emperor not forged this knife, could you shave willow with a finger or bite it with your teeth?

sentences.zh: 凡此土地人民一切諸政，皆先帝所創立。

translations.literal: All these lands, peoples, and every policy were established by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: All this land, these people, every institution—were the late emperor's creation.

sentences.zh: '今榜式等當以此等事相啟迪，毋妄議前人為也。」

translations.literal: Now you bangshi ought to use such things to instruct one another—do not rashly criticize forebears.'"
translations.idiomatic: You bangshi should take this story to heart—do not lightly fault your predecessors.'"

sentences.zh: 既又疏論兵，略謂：「上策宜薄明都，中策先取山海。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on military affairs, briefly saying: "The best plan is to press close to the Ming capital; the middle plan is first to take Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again on war: "The best strategy is to threaten the Ming capital; the next is to seize Shanhai Pass first.

sentences.zh: 當申軍令，毋辱婦女，毋妄殺人，毋貪財物。

translations.literal: One should enforce military orders: do not dishonor women, do not kill people recklessly, do not covet goods.
translations.idiomatic: Enforce discipline: no violating women, no killing without cause, no looting.

sentences.zh: 有以離家久得財多而勸還師者，上毋為所惑。」

translations.literal: There are those who, having been long from home and gained much wealth, urge returning the army—the sovereign must not be deluded by them."
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed those who, grown rich on long campaigns, plead to go home."

sentences.zh: 九年，以所屬戶口耗減，坐黜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because households under his charge had dwindled, on conviction he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 his registered households had declined, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：太祖時，儒臣未置官署。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In the Taizu period, Confucian ministers had no established office.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Under Taizu, scholar-officials had no formal bureau.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，命諸儒臣分兩直，譯曰「文館」，亦曰「書房」；

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong the Confucian ministers were ordered to divide into two shifts—translated as "Literary Bureau," also called "Study";
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year 3 they were divided into two shifts—the "Literary Bureau," also called the "Study";

sentences.zh: 置官署矣，而尚未有專官，諸儒臣皆授參將、游擊，號榜式；

translations.literal: an office was set up, yet there were still no dedicated posts; all Confucian ministers were given regimental commander and mobile brigadier ranks, titled bangshi;
translations.idiomatic: an office existed, but no dedicated posts—all were breveted regimental or brigade commanders, called bangshi;

sentences.zh: 未授官者曰「秀才」，亦曰「相公」。

translations.literal: those not yet given office were called "xiucai," also "lord secretary."
translations.idiomatic: those without military rank were "xiucai," or "lord secretary."

sentences.zh: 崇德改元，設內三院，希福、文程、承先及剛林授大學士，是為命相之始。

translations.literal: When Chongde changed the era name, the Inner Three Courts were established; Xifu, Wencheng, Chengxian, and Ganglin were appointed Grand Secretaries—this was the beginning of appointing chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: With the Chongde era came the Inner Three Courts; Xifu, Wencheng, Chengxian, and Ganglin became Grand Secretaries—the first true premiers.

sentences.zh: 希福屢奉使，履險效忱，撫輯屬部；

translations.literal: Xifu repeatedly went on missions, braved peril and showed loyalty, soothed and gathered dependent tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Xifu went on dangerous embassies again and again, loyal in peril, pacifying vassal peoples;

sentences.zh: 文程定大計，左台贊襄，佐命勳最高；

translations.literal: Wencheng settled the great design, assisted from the Left Terrace, his founding merit highest;
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng set the grand strategy and aided at court—his founding merit was supreme;

sentences.zh: 完我忠讜耿耿，歷挫折而不撓，終蒙主契；

translations.literal: Wanwo's loyal remonstrance was shining; through setbacks he did not bend, and in the end won the sovereign's trust;
translations.idiomatic: Wanwo's blunt loyalty survived every setback and won the emperor's trust at last;

sentences.zh: 承先以完我薦直文館，而先完我入相，參預軍畫。

translations.literal: Chengxian entered the Literary Bureau on Wanwo's recommendation, yet Wanwo entered the chancellorship first; Chengxian joined in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian entered the Literary Bureau on Wanwo's word; Wanwo reached the premiership first, but Chengxian shared in war planning.

sentences.zh: 間除敵帥，皆有經綸。

translations.literal: When they removed enemy commanders in turn, each showed statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Each time they brought down an enemy leader, they showed true statecraft.

sentences.zh: 草昧之績，視蕭、曹、房、杜，殆無不及也。

translations.literal: Their achievements in the primal chaos, compared with Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui, perhaps are not inferior.
translations.idiomatic: In founding a realm from nothing, they scarcely fall short of Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui.
